topics.title: Post-installation checklist
steps: Visually check wiring matches the installation manual (section 3.2 Cable connection).
Disconnect switch is ON.
Circuit breaker is ON.
Battery “ON” LED is ON.
Inverter power is ON.
Inverter has the latest firmware.
Inverter recognises the battery.
Battery can operate after installation: AC grid connected, meter installed, government approval complete.
notes: If any of the above checks fail, or the inverter needs to be turned off, turn OFF the circuit breaker first.

images.caption: Serial number label location

topics.title: Basic power cycle / reset
steps: Turn off the PV system: Inverter AC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Battery DC Isolator.
Open the bottom-right door in front of the battery (behind the HV cover / wiring cover) to access the 5-Pole CB and 2-Pole CB.
Turn OFF the 5-Pole CB (down position), then the 2-Pole CB (left position).
Wait a solid one minute.
Turn ON the 2-Pole CB (right position), then the 5-Pole CB (up position).
Wait a solid one minute and observe the battery LEDs: is FAULT lit? Does it shut down within 15–20 seconds? Does it stay on?
notes: If the FAULT light comes on, capture video of the battery tripping and email it to [contact email removed].

If the battery does NOT trip, it is fine — the issue is external to the battery. Proceed to turn the rest of the system back on (Battery DC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Inverter AC Isolator) and allow up to 10 minutes for the system to fire back up.
Compare inverter lights/screen data to a photo taken before you started, to confirm it matches the pre-fault state.

images.caption: Battery disconnect switch (1) and circuit breaker (2) locations

topics.title: On + FAULT light together (2 scenarios)
steps: This fault has two possible causes: the battery is discharged below its recommended state of charge, OR the battery is genuinely faulty.
Make sure the inverter is off and the battery is disconnected from the inverter; CB and AUX power switch OFF.
Remove the top cover (pry up back corners), then the inner top cover (10mm socket), then lift the top cover and remove the inner metal plate with a ratchet.
Check fuse continuity with a multimeter.
Ensure the 2-Pole CB is ON and the 5-Pole CB is OFF, then measure DC voltage at the Anderson Plug.

decisionTree.question: What is the measured Anderson Plug voltage?

branches.result: Issue RMA. Investigate root cause: was the inverter replaced? Any rectification work performed? Any event that caused the SOC to drop (inverter malfunction/misconfiguration, maintenance work, prolonged load without charging source, high load demand, loose/faulty connections)?
Send a charger form; once approved, send an HV charger and follow the manual charging procedure.
Verify with SolarEdge whether they can force-charge the battery. If they cannot, request a charger.

branches.when: ≥ 130V but battery still trips when isolated (Scenario 2)
branches.result: Issue an RMA and capture photos/video for the RMA submission.

images.caption: LED reference: Power on / Charging / Discharging / Fault states

topics.title: Battery shows no lights at all
steps: Two likely causes: a blown fuse, or the battery is in sleep mode.
Isolate: inverter off, battery disconnected from inverter, CB & AUX switch OFF.
Remove top cover, inner top cover, lift top cover, remove inner metal plate.
Check fuse continuity with a multimeter.

decisionTree.question: Is the fuse blown?

branches.result: Request LGES/SSG team to send out two replacement fuses. Collect end-user name, contact and address for shipping. Advise the customer to contact the installer once the fuses arrive.

branches.when: Fuse is continuous, but still no lights after a power cycle
branches.result: Likely sleep mode. Perform an isolation test to confirm. Send the fuse out in advance (in case) and merge the technician call with SolarEdge — ask SolarEdge to wake the battery by changing the battery profile.

notes: If a battery keeps repeatedly blowing fuses, this points to a deeper system-level issue (often the inverter or system config) — see ‘Repeated blown fuses’ topic below.

images.caption: LED reference: Power on / Charging / Discharging / Fault states

topics.title: Repeated blown fuses – deeper investigation
steps: 1. Inspect the inverter: check for a blown DC fuse, overheating/damaged/loose DC terminals, and that input voltages are within spec.
2. Check fault codes: log in to the inverter monitoring portal; review fault/error history for DC overcurrent, ground faults or communication failures.
3. Review site history: has more than one battery been replaced at this site? Any pattern across inverter, cabling or site conditions?
4. Verify system configuration: correct battery type/inverter compatibility; CAN/RS485 comms cabling secure and terminated; check battery orientation, wiring order and isolator polarity.
5. Electrical testing (installer/electrician): GND-AUX to BAT-ENABLE and RS485H to RS485L should read 200–400mV; CAN_H to CAN_L and EN_H to EN_G should read 8–12V.
6. Investigate external factors: recent electrical work, grid instability, lightning/surge events, water ingress, grounding/surge protection.
7. If unresolved, escalate to technical support with all test results, photos, serial numbers and a clear timeline.

topics.title: Blinking ON light
steps: Isolate the battery (disconnect DC terminals and comms cable at the battery end).
Switch the CBs ON and observe the lights.
If all lights are flashing while isolated → corrupted firmware.
Ask the installer whether the inverter or its components were replaced, and check with the inverter manufacturer whether firmware was flashed from the inverter side.
Turn off CBs, lift the top cover, remove the inner metal plate, check fuse continuity, then unplug the Anderson plug and measure voltage with the 2-Pole CB ON.

decisionTree.question: What is the measured Anderson Plug voltage?

branches.result: Firmware update only is required (firmware likely corrupted, not a hardware fault). Inform the installer the battery needs a reflash at the warehouse — arrange shipping at the customer’s expense.

images.caption: LED reference: Power on / Charging / Discharging / Fault states

topics.title: Low Anderson Plug voltage (remote check via SolarEdge)
steps: Acquire fault logs from SolarEdge.
Verify telemetry for BatteryVoltage (Anderson Plug Voltage) — normal range is 120V–130V DC.
If Anderson Plug Voltage is < 125V, an HV Charger Form needs to be issued. Also follow the ‘On + FAULT light’ (Scenario 1) procedure above.

If required, ask SolarEdge to change the minimum SOC (after a power cycle) and the minimum backup power to force the inverter to charge the battery from the grid up to that mark; remaining charge comes from excess solar (Maximum Self Consumption profile).
Ask the customer/installer to monitor the site afterwards.

images.caption: Anderson plug / fuse compartment — access panel

topics.title: Blinking Discharge light
steps: Ask the installer to verify the battery still functions >10 minutes after being isolated.
Check if the battery serial number is recognised by the inverter via the LCD button.
Ask the installer to verify the inverter fuses with SolarEdge.

decisionTree.question: Is the inverter fuse blown?

branches.result: Raise it with the SolarEdge team and isolate the battery to preserve its state of charge.

Check for inverter errors on the SolarEdge portal. Verify comms cables on battery/inverter for looseness. Check EN_H/EN_G (expect 8–12V) and RS485H/RS485L (expect 400mV–1V). Request SolarEdge for the battery fault log, then create a ticket and escalate.

topics.title: Anderson Plug check – suspected blown fuse
steps: Inverter off; ask technician to switch off and isolate the battery; CB & AUX power switch OFF.
Disconnect battery cables from the inverter.
Remove top cover, inner top cover, lift top cover, remove inner metal plate.
Check the battery fuses.
If blown → request LGES/SSG team send two replacement fuses, and collect end-user shipping details.
Bypass the fuse to check SOC at the Anderson plug: with the 2-Pole CB ON and 5-Pole CB OFF, place one multimeter probe on the left side of the fuse and the other on the 2-Pole CB black screw.

decisionTree.question: What is the SOC / voltage reading when bypassing the fuse?

branches.result: Send the RMA. Investigate why the battery discharged below 0V and whether the inverter was replaced or rectification work was performed.

Anderson plug / fuse compartment — access panel

topics.title: Identifying and photographing swelling
steps: Take a photo of the entire battery, standing in front of it.
Take a zoomed-in photo of the lower half of the battery.
Take photos of the serial number (both locations).
Take a photo of the entire setup, and check system clearances.
Send all photos to [contact email removed].
Assess/measure the degree of swelling.

decisionTree.question: How much has the case swollen?

branches.result: Ask the installer to switch the battery OFF, then issue RMA.
Leave the battery ON, then issue RMA.

notes: Document swelling thoroughly with photos before lodging the claim.

devices.name: LG RESU LV Battery (3.2EX / 6.4EX / 6.5 / 10 / 12 / 13 / Plus)
devices.summary: Low-voltage LG RESU battery range, commonly paired with Sungrow, SolaX and GoodWe inverters. RESU Plus is the combiner unit for pairing two LV packs.

topics.title: Power cycle – RESU 3.2EX / 6.4EX
steps: Turn off the PV system: Inverter AC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Battery DC Isolator.
Remove the black top cover using a 4mm Allen key.
Check the Battery Circuit Breaker position — if aligned in the middle, the battery is tripped.
If not already tripped, turn the Circuit Breaker OFF (0 position).
Wait a solid one minute.
Turn the Circuit Breaker back ON (1 position) and observe the battery for one minute.
notes: The customer themselves can perform this power cycle; any further testing requires their supplier or a licensed electrician.
If it does not trip, it's fine — the issue is external to the battery. Proceed to turn the rest of the system back on and allow ~10 minutes to recover.
If the FAULT light comes on, capture video and email [contact email removed].

Checklist while observing: are battery lights visible? Is it communicating with the inverter? Any new error codes? Is it charging/discharging correctly as load changes? Does SOC update? Do app/portal show correct data?

topics.title: Power cycle – RESU 6.5 / 10 / 12 / 13
steps: For safety, the customer must NOT remove the battery top cover on these models — a licensed electrician should be engaged if needed.
Turn off the PV system: Inverter AC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Battery DC Isolator.
Remove the black top cover with a 4mm Allen key.
Check/clear the Circuit Breaker position as above, wait one minute, then switch back ON.
The battery should stay on for 10 minutes when isolated from the inverter with no fault light — this indicates no battery issue.
notes: If the battery trips with a fault light, or won't charge/discharge, further investigation is required — capture video, send to [contact email removed], and inspect inverter error logs with photos.

topics.title: CB tripping or no communication – decision tree
steps: First establish: is this a NEW installation (commissioning) or an OLD/EXISTING installation that was working before?

decisionTree.question: New installation or old/existing installation?

branches.result: Check number of batteries and set DIP switches to match (see cable/DIP guide). Check the RJ45 communication slot location. Inspect DC polarity, communication wiring, short circuits, reverse polarity, external equipment faults and incorrect inverter fuse rating. SolaX: inverter pins 1 & 2. Sungrow: inverter pins 4 & 5. Replace the RJ45 cable if required. If all checks pass, proceed with the RMA.

Check if system is ON; review inverter fault codes/history. Disconnect the battery from the inverter to rule out external influence. Measure DC terminal voltage. If the isolator is ON but there are no lights or DC terminals read 0V, this confirms a blown fuse (see Blown Fuse topic). If none of this resolves it, proceed with an RMA.

notes: Old-installation voltage sub-check: DC Voltage ≥ 45V → isolate and turn battery back on — if it trips within 5 seconds, it's faulty → RMA. If DC Voltage < 45V, SOC is effectively 0%: if ≥ 42V, force charge may be possible; if < 42V, force charge is not possible → faulty battery → issue RMA.
Battery trip time in this fault is typically under a minute. Likely causes beyond a faulty battery: DIP switch misconfiguration, or a communication wiring problem.

images.caption: RJ45 data port — correct port note

topics.title: Blown fuse (LV battery)
steps: Check DIP switches are at the recommended (black/default) position.
Check voltage across the DC terminals — 0V can indicate a faulty fuse.
Check for a short circuit (dead short) across the inverter terminals.
Take photos of the battery DC terminal voltage.
Send photos to [contact email removed] and submit the RMA.
notes: Note the probable cause of the blown fuse: inverter dead short, wrong connection, external equipment fault, or a short circuit in wiring/system.

topics.title: Swelling (LV battery)
steps: Take a photo of the entire battery, serial number, and the entire setup/clearances.
Send photos to [contact email removed].
Evaluate degree of swelling.

decisionTree.question: How much has the case swollen?

branches.result: Ask the installer to switch the battery off, then raise RMA.
Leave the battery on, then raise RMA.

notes: A separate note in the same source guide says to “raise an RMA only if swelling exceeds 2mm” — this is inconsistent with the >5mm / <3mm guidance above. Treat 2mm as the conservative trigger point and confirm borderline cases with the LG team.
Also check inverter fault logs where possible (Sungrow Fault Records, SolaX Error Records).

topics.title: Cell imbalance
steps: Stand in front of the inverter, photograph it, and check its fault code.
notes: Inverter fault codes indicating cell imbalance — Sungrow: Fault 937, 868. SolaX: “Batt Cell Imbalance”. GoodWe/LG: contact GoodWe for logs, refer to LGES.

topics.title: Deep discharged battery
steps: Check the DC voltage across the DC terminals and compare to the expected charge level band for the inverter brand.
notes: Battery charge level bands: Sungrow 32V–70V. SolaX 40V–60V. LGES and GoodWe 40V–60V.

images.caption: Measuring terminal block voltage — do not use battery below 38V

topics.title: Status light blinking – RESU 6.4EX
steps: Photograph the whole system (inverter + battery status lights).
Check the inverter fault code. If no inverter-side fault, check the battery status lights.
If lights blink green/orange, check DC voltage at the battery DC terminals.

decisionTree.question: Is DC voltage within 45.2V – 58.1V?

branches.when: Yes (voltage is within the normal range, yet lights are still blinking)
branches.result: Battery can be deemed faulty — send RMA.

images.caption: Role of the LED — RESU 6.4EX front panel

topics.title: RESU 3.2EX connected with 6.4EX
steps: Photograph the inverter and check its fault code.
Check the connections between the RESU 6.4EX and RESU 3.2EX.
If no inverter-side fault, check battery status lights and fuse continuity on the RESU 3.2EX.
notes: If the fuse is blown, the status light blinks orange and green. Send RMA.
If a RESU3.2EX is found faulty, the ENTIRE combination (both packs) requires replacement.
3.2EX batteries have no LED lights of their own; with two stacks, connect one stack at a time to isolate the fault.

images.caption: RESU battery combination compatibility matrix

topics.title: RESU Plus – connection, DIP switches & combiner setup
steps: RESU Plus combines two 48V (LV series) RESU packs in pairs. Only RESU13s can be combined with each other.
Mount: remove front cover, loosen corner screws, remove circuit board carefully (don't separate it from its metal plate).
Wiring: before connecting any cables, ensure inverter and battery packs are OFF. Lower-left terminal block = pack 1 DC, lower-right = pack 2 DC, upper = inverter.
Pay close attention to polarity — reverse polarity can severely damage the battery pack.
Selectronic inverters: RESU Plus DIP switches should be CAN_H-1, CAN_L-2, GND-3, or you will see a battery communication error.
Set RESU Plus DIP switches to 0011; set both battery packs' DIP switches to 0010.
Connect ground wires, 12V power cable (White = Positive, Black = Negative), and network/CAN-bus cables per the terminal mapping.

Finalise: confirm DIP switches on RESU Plus and both packs, switch packs ON (should power up in < 30 seconds), confirm ON indicator on the pack and Pack 1/2 indicators on RESU Plus (Fault indicator may flash briefly while both batteries initialise), then turn on the inverter.
notes: Always complete a software update when replacing batteries, so the RESU Plus firmware stays compatible.

images.caption: RESU Plus DIP switch bank (1–4)
RESU Plus combiner wiring (red/blue leads)

topics.title: RESU Plus – software update procedure
steps: Requires a Class 4, 16GB SD card (the ‘4’ in a circle confirms Class 4).
Upload the .hex firmware file to an empty SD card.
Turn off the inverter, open the flap on the left of the RESU Plus and insert the SD card.
Remove the network cable from both the battery and inverter sides of the RESU Plus.
Only one battery's power cable needs to stay connected during the update; set that single battery's DIP switch to 0011.
Turn the battery on, then press and hold the Update button beside the card slot for 3+ seconds.
LEDs flash in cycles for up to 1 minute. Success = only the ON indicator lights; failure = Fault indicator flashes for 2 seconds (recheck the card and retry).
After success: turn off the battery, reconnect both batteries with DIP switches back to 0010, remove the SD card, close the flap, and turn the inverter back on.

images.caption: RESU Plus firmware update screen
RESU Plus SD card for firmware update

devices.name: LG Prime HV Battery (Enblock Manager)
devices.summary: LG Prime HV battery, commissioned and maintained through the LG “Enblock Manager” mobile app.

topics.title: Power cycle
steps: Turn off the PV system: Inverter AC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Battery DC Isolator.
Open the battery's top door — it holds the circuit breaker switch.
Turn the circuit breaker OFF, wait a solid one minute, then turn it back ON.
Wait another minute and observe: lights state, FAULT light, does it trip in the first 15–20 seconds, does it stay on?
notes: If it trips with FAULT on, capture video and send to [contact email removed].
If it doesn't trip, the issue is external — restore the rest of the system (PV Array DC isolator, then Inverter AC isolator) and allow 10 minutes to recover.

images.caption: Battery Control Unit LED / fault indicator location

topics.title: High-pitch noise – battery firmware update
steps: Open the Enblock Manager app.

Without logging in: tap “Battery FW Update” on the login page, select a region, download the firmware, then scan the battery's QR code (S/N prefix EH257064P8S or EH153064P8S) to walk through: scan → enter product info → check battery status → FW update.
If logged in: Open Enblock Manager → “Direct Connection Battery” → “Battery Status” → connect to the battery → check status, then run the FW update from the registered system list.
notes: When FW update completes for each device (RMD/BMS/DCDC) the app sometimes disconnects and auto-reconnects; reconnect manually if that fails.

images.caption: Firmware update — SSID connection step

topics.title: Error 3X82 after battery replacement
steps: Power down: Inverter AC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Battery DC Isolator; open the battery's top door and cycle the circuit breaker OFF then ON; confirm module directions.
Error 3X82 occurs from a firmware mismatch or missing firmware.

In Enblock Manager: if the battery was never commissioned, complete full commissioning. If the site had an old battery registered, use Maintenance → Replacement to update the site with the new battery.
Once commissioned (new or replacement), it automatically receives the latest firmware: RMD 4.2.1, BMS 2.6.3.4, DCDC 1.4.0.0 (as recommended by LGES), which removes the mismatch causing 3X82.
After the update, confirm the 3X82 error is gone, then power the system back up in order.
notes: Even if combined module voltage looks low (~100V), the battery should still charge from grid or excess solar.
If the error persists, recheck the firmware update logs in Enblock Manager or contact LG technical support.

topics.title: Blown fuse
steps: Turn off the PV system (Inverter AC → PV Array DC → Battery DC isolators) and the circuit breaker.
Remove power/sensing connectors from both modules (visual inspection before proceeding) — do NOT lift the Battery Control Unit (BCU) until all connectors are disconnected.
Remove the handle plate and fuse cover.
Set a multimeter to resistance and check the fuse.

decisionTree.question: What is the fuse resistance?

branches.result: Expected value is 0.2 ± 0.1 Ω. Reassemble in reverse order.
The entire battery must be replaced — a single blown fuse on any module means full battery replacement.

images.caption: Blown fuse — multimeter resistance test wiring

topics.title: Voltage leakage
steps: Symptom: battery does not charge or discharge properly.
Turn off the PV system; isolate the battery (remove power and comms cables), then turn off the circuit breaker.
Wait a full five minutes.

Turn the circuit breaker back on and measure DC voltage across the terminals (battery and inverter should be OFF during this measurement, with the inter-connecting cable removed). The reading is the leakage voltage.

decisionTree.question: What is the measured leakage voltage?

branches.result: Fine — no action needed.
Voltage leakage confirmed → issue RMA.
Verify with the LGES team before deciding.

images.caption: Battery power terminal layout (+POS / GND / -NEG)

topics.title: Cable connection & DIP switch configuration guide
steps: Section A – inverter communication ports: enable-ground to Terminal 2, enable-12V-positive to Terminal 1; RS-485 (A+, B-) to Terminals 3 & 4, or CAN (high, low) to Terminals 5 & 6 depending on the inverter's protocol.

Sections B/C – termination resistor DIP switches: single pack → switch ON (lowered). Two packs with the inverter having two separate comm ports → turn ON both packs' termination resistors. Two packs sharing one comm port → primary pack termination ON (last in the daisy chain), secondary pack termination OFF (middle of the chain).

Section E – battery power port: positive/negative lines join at the combiner box; reversed polarity means the system will not operate normally. Loose power cables can arc and damage the battery and/or inverter.

Primary / secondary pack — terminating resistor switch setting

devices.name: LGES 5048 Inverter (GoodWe platform)
devices.summary: LGES-branded hybrid inverter built on the GoodWe platform, managed through the GoodWe IoT Smart Management Platform and PV Master app.

topics.title: Wi-Fi / dongle troubleshooting
steps: Symptom: if the inverter loses internet, the battery SOC (%) shown in the app stops updating and just holds its last value.
Check the inverter's Wi-Fi LED indicator. Request a power cycle of the system.
Verify the inverter recognises the dongle (solid blue Wi-Fi light). If not, remove and reinsert the dongle (small clip, may need a screwdriver).
If the dongle has a reload button, press and hold it for 10 seconds (or 30 seconds via the meter plate reload button for a full Wi-Fi forget/reconfigure).

decisionTree.question: What's the specific Wi-Fi symptom?

branches.result: Confirm inverter is powered and the Wi-Fi module is attached. Move the smart device closer. Restart the inverter. Press “Wi-Fi Reload” to return to default mode and reconfigure.
Try password 12345678. Check nothing else is already connected to it. Press “Wi-Fi Reload” and reconfigure. Restart the inverter. Check for unacceptable characters in your chosen password.
Press “Wi-Fi Reload” and reconfigure. Switch to Chrome, Firefox, IE or Safari.
Move the router closer or use a Wi-Fi repeater. If the router's Wi-Fi channel number is higher than 13, lower it in the router's settings.
Restart the inverter. Re-check SSID/encryption method/password match the router exactly. Check the router hasn't hit its device limit. Restart the router. Move the router closer or add a repeater.
Connect a smart device to a different Wi-Fi network and check the LGES eMonitoring Portal to see if the inverter shows online. Restart both the router and inverter.

branches.when: Inverter shows Offline on the LGES eMonitoring Portal
branches.result: Wait a few minutes for data transmission and re-check later. Confirm a solid blue Wi-Fi light on the inverter. Ask the installer to open the meter plate and hold the reload button for 30 seconds. If the LED still isn't stable, the inverter may have forgotten the Wi-Fi — reconfigure it from scratch.
Check LED indicators, power cycle, confirm solid blue light, connect via PV Master app if still offline, and once back online proceed with the standard firmware update procedure.

notes: Dongle lights: yellow = powered on, blue = active communication. Both on = inverter is successfully connected to the customer's internet.

T568B RJ45 pinout reference

topics.title: Firmware update (ARM + Master/DSP)
steps: Go to the GoodWe IoT Smart Management Platform (au.iot.goodwe-power.com) → Device Management → Flash tab → Flash Query → New.

ARM update first: get the update file from the LG Dropbox, enter the inverter S/N with an ‘A’ prefix (to signify the ARM update), and submit. The inverter must be online for the update to start; track progress in the Flash Progress column until 100%.
Then do the MASTER/DSP update the same way, entering the S/N without the ‘A’ prefix and submitting the DSP file.

topics.title: IoT parameter quick reference
steps: Only one parameter can be saved at a time (select the radio button next to it, then Save).
App Mode Index: 0 = General, 1 = False Off Grid, 2 = Backup Mode, 3 = Eco Mode.
Anti-Reverse Current toggles export limiting; Power Limit sets the export cap (max 5000W).
PV Start Voltage default is 150V.
GridWaveCheckLevel: Default = 0. If backup is flickering and dropping grid, try setting 1 or 2.
EMSPower: 0 = 3rd Party Controller present, 1 = No 3rd Party Controller.

CT wiring: CT A→L1, CT B→L2, CT C→L3, following the House→Grid direction; the CT direction cannot be reversed and the 3m CT cable must not be extended. One Smart Meter per LGES inverter; three CTs if three-phase.
notes: Changing Backup Enable, discharge windows, battery model, or safety region settings should be done carefully — Safety region options for Australia: A = VIC/SA/NSW/QLD, B = WA, C = TAS.

images.caption: Communication pin color / function reference

topics.title: BMS Comm Failure
steps: Fault: the lithium battery and inverter cannot communicate.
1. Confirm BMS comms cable sequence matches the install manual and the connection tests normal (CAN or RS-485 per battery mode).
2. Confirm the battery model selected in PV Master matches reality.
3. If ET + BYD HV battery: confirm the battery is connected to its own Wi-Fi and configured for cell count / inverter manufacturer / protocol (requires BYD firmware ≥ V3.012R).
4. Measure the battery's output voltage at the inverter side with a multimeter; confirm polarity.
5. (ET only) Confirm battery power cable polarity is not reversed — ET has polarity protection for HV batteries but not for LV battery inverters; reversed LV connections can damage the inverter.
6. (Alpha-ESS only) Confirm the inverter shipped as the active version, not passive — correct via calibration tool (offline) or remotely through GoodWe service (if on SEMS).
7. If all of the above check out, the fault is likely the inverter's BMS communication port — contact the GoodWe service team.

images.caption: Battery terminal assembly (waterproof ring / cable / insulator / screw cap)

topics.title: Meter Comm Failure
steps: Fault: the meter and inverter cannot communicate.
1. Confirm the meter comms cable sequence matches the install manual.
2. If unplugging the BMS comms cable restores meter comms, the BMS cable needs modification (only CAN-H/CAN-L should remain).
3. Confirm the meter model matches the inverter — replace with the GoodWe smart meter if an Ancrel three-phase meter (DTSD1352) is fitted.
4. (Alpha-ESS only) Confirm active vs passive inverter version as above.
5. If the meter itself is suspected faulty, replace it.
6. If all checks pass, contact the GoodWe service team — likely an inverter-side meter communication port issue.

images.caption: Meter / CT wiring panel
Meter CT wiring — check point

topics.title: Abnormal Battery Charging
steps: Fault: the battery fails to charge, or doesn't charge at normal power.
1. Check BMS fault code — handle per BMS Comm Failure solutions if abnormal.
2. Check PV Master advanced settings for a charging current upper limit.
3. Lead-acid batteries: check capacity setting — charging current = battery capacity × 0.15.
4. Check BMS charging current limit via PV Master monitoring data — this is expected behaviour, explain to the customer, no action needed.
5. Check SOC and BMS charge-overvoltage alarm — if the battery is simply full, explain to the customer, no action needed.
6. Check meter communication status — handle per Meter Comm Failure if abnormal.
7. Confirm the inverter isn't set to Economic Mode charging/discharging on a user-set schedule — adjust via PV Master/remote control if needed.
8. Check the safety curve setting — grid voltage/frequency may be triggering a curve; disable if not required locally.
9. If PV voltage is too high, reduce the number of strings to bring it into normal range.
10. If all 9 steps check out, contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: Abnormal Battery Discharging
steps: Fault: the battery fails to discharge, or doesn't discharge at normal power. Follow the same step pattern as Abnormal Battery Charging (BMS fault code, PV Master discharge current limits, battery capacity setting, SOC/undervoltage alarm, meter comms, work mode, safety curve), escalating to GoodWe service if none resolve it.

topics.title: Inverter LED is off – cannot power on
steps: 1. Check the inverter DC switch is ON.
2. If connected to PV only: measure open-circuit string voltage. It must reach the inverter's minimum starting voltage; if it does and the inverter still won't start after 5–10 minutes, continue.
3. Check for reverse polarity on any DC string with a multimeter (red lead to positive, black to negative) — rectify on site if found.
4. If connected to battery only: the battery voltage must be above a minimum threshold for the inverter to start.

5. If connected to AC only: measure voltage at the on-grid terminal. If no voltage, check/rectify the on-grid cabling. If voltage is present and it still won't power on, contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: DC Injection High | Error 29
steps: Fault: DC injection from the inverter is too high during output.
South Africa and Italy have strict DC injection requirements that may need remote parameter adjustment.
Upgrade to the latest DSP firmware* (requires GoodWe engineer approval). If the error persists after upgrading, contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: Relay Check | Error 29
steps: Fault: the inverter detected a relay fault.
1. Power off AC & DC, measure voltage between neutral and ground at the on-grid side — should be ≤ 10V; if higher, grounding is poor and needs correcting.
2. Measure resistance between neutral and ground at the backup side — should be < 10Ω.
3. Restart the inverter — if it starts normally, the error was AC-voltage disturbance (no action needed). If it still won't start, contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: Reconnecting / self-test loop
steps: Fault: the auto self-test fails and keeps looping.
1. Confirm the inverter's selected safety regulations match local grid requirements.
2. Confirm each PV string reaches the inverter's minimum starting voltage (check via PV Master).
3. Measure N-to-ground voltage at both the on-grid and backup sides — should be < 10V (poor grounding if ≥ 10V).
4. Pull the AC cable outward to confirm it's well-terminated.
5. Check the specific warning code shown and contact the GoodWe service team with that code if unresolved.

topics.title: Waiting for Power Generation
steps: Fault: PV voltage has reached starting voltage, but the inverter isn't generating power.
1. Confirm the inverter is connected to at least two power sources (PV, battery, AC) — a storage inverter needs at least two to connect to grid.
2. Confirm selected safety regulations match local grid requirements.
3. Confirm each string reaches minimum starting voltage.
4. Check the specific warning code on PV Master and contact GoodWe with that code if needed.
5. For Australia (DRED) or EU (remote shutdown): confirm the required terminal/resistor is fitted (15kΩ DRED resistor for Australian inverters) — contact GoodWe if missing.

topics.title: Terminal Burnt (AC or DC)
steps: Work through each check in order — several outcomes affect warranty status:
1. Was a non-standard (non-GoodWe) DC connector used? If yes → warranty void.
2. Were DC terminals crimped to the user manual's requirements? If not → warranty void.
3. Reverse polarity on any DC string that caused the burn? If yes → site must be rectified; warranty void for that cause.
4. Cross-wiring between DC strings? If found, rectify on site.
5. Poor AC terminal crimping? If yes → warranty void.
6/7. AC cable material/diameter not meeting the manual's requirements (e.g. aluminium without copper-aluminium terminals, or undersized cable)? If so → warranty void.
8. Open the inverter and check the SPD (surge protection device) for lightning-strike damage — if damaged, it's a lightning event and beyond warranty.
If none of the above apply, contact the GoodWe service team to confirm the solution.

images.caption: Battery terminal torque / direction reference

topics.title: Water inside the inverter
steps: 1. Check all used terminals are connected and tight, unused terminals are blocked, and external sealing screws are tight. If sealing is poor, this is an installation defect (not to manual spec) — warranty void.
2. Open the cover and check for stagnant water inside. If present, contact the GoodWe service team.
3. Check for condensation. If it's affecting function, contact GoodWe; if it's not affecting function, it can usually clear itself in good weather.

topics.title: Utility Loss | Error 23
steps: Fault: inverter detects no AC voltage / voltage below the safety threshold.
1. Confirm other equipment on the same grid connection works normally — if not, it's a grid/mains issue; contact an electrician or the grid company.
2. Check the inverter's upper AC switch is closed and not damaged (compare voltage above/below the switch).
3. Check AC wiring/termination by gently pulling the cable.
4. Check the over/under-voltage protector isn't tripped or wired backwards (its upper end must connect to the grid).
5. With AC and DC shut down, measure impedance between live and neutral — should be > 200kΩ (much lower suggests internal continuity — contact GoodWe HQ).
6. Measure voltage between neutral and ground — should be ≤ 10V.
7. Check for a reversed neutral/live connection on the AC side.
If all pass, contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: Low Generation
steps: 1. Check anti-reverse / over-frequency load reduction / PU curve / slope loading functions aren't unnecessarily limiting output — disable per local requirements if so.
2. Measure grid voltage/frequency — if close to the safety regulation's upper limit, it may be triggering derating; try switching the safety regulation to 50/60Hz Default.
3. Test string open-circuit voltage/short-circuit current against the module's label spec — mismatch suggests a module-side problem.
4. Check installation environment: shading, PV array tilt/azimuth, dirt/debris on panels, hot spots/cracks in modules, or an enclosed (overheating) inverter location.

5. Turn on high-power appliances at midday and watch whether inverter output increases — if not, the power-distribution cabinet's cable diameter may be too thin (limited transmission capacity). If output does increase as expected, contact GoodWe to confirm.

topics.title: ISO Failure (insulation resistance)
steps: Fault: suspected component problem — insulation resistance to ground is < 100kΩ.
1. Confirm module type (crystalline silicon vs thin film) — thin film needs GoodWe confirmation.
2. Check grounding resistance between module frame and metal bracket — should be ≤ 10Ω.
3. Connect one string at a time to isolate which string (if any) causes the fault — if it only occurs with ALL strings connected, or on specific strings, contact GoodWe to confirm.
4. Measure cable-to-ground impedance per string — should be ≥ 10Ω (cable insulation); for HV battery power line to ground, should be ≥ 1MΩ (500kΩ minimum after repair).
5. Visually inspect module cable surface for damage.
6. Check AC-side grounding (N and ground wires) — should measure < 10Ω.

topics.title: Ground I | Error 22 / 32 (leakage current)
steps: Fault: detected leakage current is large.
1. If the fault only appears in rainy weather or morning/evening, it's likely high-humidity parasitic capacitance — self-clears on a sunny day.
2. On a sunny day: check DC (module/bracket, should be ≤ 10Ω) and AC (ground wire to grid-tie copper bar, should be ≤ 10Ω) grounding.
3. Plug/unplug each string in turn to isolate a faulty string.
4. For HV battery systems, measure impedance of the HV battery power line to ground — should be ≥ 1Ω.
5. Disconnect the battery (leave only PV + grid) — if it connects to grid normally, the battery cable insulation is the problem; check/correct it.

topics.title: VAC Failure (grid overvoltage)
steps: Fault: grid voltage exceeded the inverter's safety requirement. Follow a similar check sequence to Utility Loss: grid condition, AC switch/wiring, grounding, then escalate to GoodWe if unresolved.

topics.title: Grid Frequency fault
steps: Fault: grid frequency exceeds the range permitted by the inverter's safety regulations. Confirm the correct safety regulation/country set, check for genuine grid frequency fluctuation, and escalate to GoodWe if the condition is not a real grid event.

topics.title: DC Overvoltage (low-voltage battery hybrid)
steps: Fault: DC string input voltage exceeds the inverter's allowable range (LV-battery hybrid inverters).

1. Power off and disconnect all PV strings; measure open-circuit voltage of each string and calculate the maximum expected Voc for the actual configuration and local climate. If max Voc exceeds the inverter's DC voltage range, reduce the panel count per string.

2. Compare PV-side voltage (multimeter) to the value shown on PV Master — mismatch means a sampling/calibration issue (needs calibration tool, or a control board replacement on ES models) — escalate to GoodWe if unresolved.

topics.title: DC Overvoltage (high-voltage battery hybrid)
steps: Fault: DC string input voltage exceeds the inverter's allowable range (HV-battery hybrid inverters, e.g. ET).
1. As above — check string Voc vs the inverter's max DC range; reduce panel count if exceeded.
2. Compare PV-side voltage reading to PV Master's displayed value — calibrate or replace control board (ET only) if mismatched.
3. Check battery voltage against the inverter's DC voltage range — reduce the number of batteries, or contact the battery vendor, if exceeded.
4. Compare battery-side voltage to PV Master's displayed value — calibrate, replace control board, or contact GoodWe if still mismatched.

topics.title: Over Temperature
steps: 1. Confirm installation location meets the user manual's clearance/ventilation requirements — reinstall correctly if not.
2. Measure ambient temperature around the inverter — if over 45°C, cool the environment.
3. If ambient is under 45°C, power off for 15 minutes then restart — if it then runs normally, it was a temporary high-temperature event; if it still fails, contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: EEP ROM read/write failure
steps: Fault: control board storage chip read/write failure. If the inverter runs normally after a restart, no further action is required; otherwise contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: DC Bus voltage too high
steps: Fault: internal DC bus voltage inside the device is too high. This is largely an internal hardware condition — confirm it isn't tied to a DC overvoltage event upstream, otherwise contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: AC output current sensor failure
steps: Internal hardware fault — contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: Control board malfunction (indicator abnormal)
steps: The control board is malfunctioning, causing an indicator to behave abnormally. This is an internal hardware fault — contact the GoodWe service team.

topics.title: Internal inductance noise
steps: 1. Confirm the selected safety regulation matches local grid requirements (mismatches can cause audible switching noise).
2. Measure the actual noise on site with a decibel meter or smartphone app and record video/audio.

decisionTree.question: Is the measured noise above 55dB?

branches.result: Contact the GoodWe service team for a solution.
This is normal operating noise for the internal inductor during power generation — no fault.

topics.title: Backup not working
steps: 1. Verify a common neutral cable is present between the grid and backup circuit.
2. Confirm sufficient grid-side voltage at the inverter (200V–240V is acceptable).
3. Get screenshots of recent performance in the LGES Monitoring app (production, consumption, battery SOC, battery cycling).
4. Confirm the backup function was switched ON at commissioning (PV Master app, iOS/Android, or the GoodWe IoT platform).

5. If still unresolved: re-check the common neutral cable, measure grid-side voltage (200–240V), simulate a blackout (turn off main grid supply and PV), then measure voltage at the inverter's backup output and photograph the reading.
notes: Watch for backup overload: if house load consistently exceeds what the backup circuit/PV can supply, the inverter will cut out every few minutes and enter self-protection, waiting progressively longer (up to 1 hour) between retries.
To force an immediate restart after resolving an overload: reduce the backup load, then in LGES PV Master go to Advanced Setting → “Reset Back-Up Overload History”.
Avoid connecting loads that need an uninterruptible supply, loads that in total exceed max backup capacity, or loads with very high start-up surge current (air-conditioners, high-power pumps).

Battery charge/discharge current can be limited by low SOC (below DOD), low battery voltage, over-temperature, or abnormal BMS communication. The inverter and battery cannot be used in a pure off-grid design.

images.caption: Backup function note — essential loads only, wattage limit
Back-up / On-grid / Grid wiring overview

topics.title: Relay Check Failure → RMA
steps: 1. Get the inverter serial number.
2. On the monitoring platform, go to Alarms, re-enter the serial number, and set the alarm status filter to “All” (active + historical).
3. Look for any “Relay Failure” alarm entries and note how often they recur.

decisionTree.question: How often has Relay Failure recurred?

branches.result: Strong indicator the inverter is faulty and may need replacement — send RMA.

topics.title: Dead Short test
steps: Turn off the inverter. The next steps must be completed within 5 minutes of shutdown.
Disconnect the battery DC cables on the inverter side.
Measure resistance across the inverter's battery terminals. Confirm battery polarity was not reversed.
Request photos from the installer (showing the inverter switched off/isolated, resistance reading, serial number sticker, and installation) and email them to [contact email removed].

decisionTree.question: What is the measured resistance?

branches.result: Dead short confirmed → raise RMA for the inverter (same process as a battery RMA). Escalate with GoodWe and request a replacement inverter; follow up regularly via the GoodWe WhatsApp chat.
Normal — no dead short.

devices.name: EM048 Stacked Battery (SolaX ecosystem)
devices.summary: Stackable LG battery modules (EM048 series) used with SolaX / SK-SU hybrid systems. Up to 10 modules per ESS rack, one designated as master.

topics.title: SolaX BMS not detected
steps: Identify whether the inverter uses External BMS Communication or Internal BMS Communication, to use the correct pin mapping.
External BMS: LG Battery CAN1 port pins 6 & 8 ↔ BMU (BMS port) pins 1 & 2. Wiring: SK-SU Pin1→LG Pin4, SK-SU Pin2→LG Pin5.
Internal BMS: LG Battery pins 6 & 8 ↔ SK-SU internal BMS pins 1 & 2. Wiring: SK-SU Pin1→LG Pin8, SK-SU Pin2→LG Pin6.
Install/commission the correct cable for the identified BMS type, verify and rectify cabling for stable communication.
Reconnect the battery, turn on the battery isolator, solar panels, then the inverter.
notes: Always keep the inverter connected to the RS-485 of the battery if there is a single battery on site.
Double-check pin positions before powering on — incorrect mapping can cause comms errors or damage the communication interface.

images.caption: BMU ↔ inverter CAN communication wiring

topics.title: Reset EM048 (reinitialise)
steps: Switch off the inverter isolator, solar panel isolator, and battery isolator.
Remove communication cables and DC cables from the battery.

Press the On/Off button on a module at the top or bottom of the rack to make it the master module (this also activates the slave modules). Green indicator lights first, then the rightmost blue indicator a few seconds later.
Press and hold the On/Off button for longer than 5 seconds — all lights turn off, meaning the battery has been reinitiated. If additional lights appear, repeat this step.
Reconnect communication and DC cables, then turn the battery isolator, solar panel isolator, and inverter isolator back on in order.

topics.title: Slave modules not activated
steps: If the master module activates normally but some slave modules don't:
Shut off the system, then deactivate the whole ESS by holding the master module's On/Off button for 5+ seconds (this removes assigned module IDs).
Check all intra-rack communication cables are properly connected between modules — use the LEFT of the two RJ-48 ports on top for intra-rack; the RIGHT port connects to the higher-level system.
Re-activate the ESS. If the problem persists, replace the communication cable.
notes: The ESS shuts itself down automatically if an error occurs during commissioning.

topics.title: Fault Number 12 (comms configuration)
steps: Symptom: red indicator on, blue indicators show fault 12 in binary.
Confirm comms settings on the higher-level system: CAN 2.0B = 500kbps, Modbus 485 = 19200bps.
Confirm pin assignments match between the higher-level system's Modbus/CAN interface and cable.
CAN protocol: fit a 120Ω resistor between CAN_L and CAN_H inside the connector to/from the higher-level system.
Modbus protocol: fit a 120Ω resistor between RTX+ and RTX− inside the connector to/from the higher-level system.
Confirm the higher-level communication cable is properly connected between the master module and the higher-level system, then re-activate the ESS.

images.caption: CAT5 RJ45 pinout for BMS/CAN connection

topics.title: Green indicator not turning on
steps: Possible causes: the module is over-discharged, or its On/Off button is faulty.
Remove the power terminal compartment cover and measure voltage at the terminal block.

decisionTree.question: What voltage is measured at the terminal block?

branches.result: Do not use this battery module. Replace the cover, and replace the module.

notes: A module ships charged to less than 25% — if the green indicator still doesn't turn on, do not use it.

images.caption: Front-panel status indicator legend (Normal/SOC/Warning/Fault 1/Fault 2)

topics.title: Blue indicators flash (mixed models)
steps: Cause: the rack contains one or more different battery module models (mixing models is not permitted).
Remove all communication cables from the modules to isolate and identify the different model(s).
Press the On/Off button to activate a module, then press-and-hold for 5+ seconds — while held, the blue indicators show the last digit of the model number in binary.
notes: The master module's blue indicators also show a model number for 10 seconds automatically: during first commissioning if mixed models are detected, or when a replacement module is a different model.

images.caption: Blue indicator binary code reference (module ID)

topics.title: Green and red indicators on simultaneously
steps: This happens whenever there's a voltage difference between any of the modules — it is expected during balancing, not necessarily a fault.
Wait for all modules to reach the same voltage; the red indicator will turn off once balanced. The lowest-voltage module charges first, then the others follow one by one.

images.caption: Front-panel status indicator legend (Normal/SOC/Warning/Fault 1/Fault 2)

topics.title: Voltage imbalance
steps: Power down in order: Inverter AC isolator → PV array DC isolator → Battery DC isolator.
Isolate the battery (disconnect DC and comms cables), then perform the standard reset procedure.
Power the battery back on and observe the LED indicators.

decisionTree.question: Do the lights still indicate a voltage imbalance after reset?

branches.result: The battery is considered faulty and requires replacement under warranty. If more than one module is installed, isolate just the module showing the imbalance and recommission the rest so master/slave roles reset and the system resumes normal operation.

images.caption: Fault condition reference — cell voltage/current/temperature deviations

topics.title: Master/slave roles & power cable wiring rules
steps: An ESS can have up to 10 modules of the SAME model — never mix models.

Whichever module (top or bottom of the rack) has its On/Off button pressed first becomes the master; it is then assigned ID 1, and communicates with the higher-level system. The rest become slaves, sequentially ID'd.
Power cables connect modules to the higher-level system via busbars — modules MUST be wired in parallel, never in series.

Make sure the higher-level system is off before wiring power cables to it. All power cables must be equal length (unequal lengths cause different resistances → voltage imbalance between modules). Total extension length from a module to the higher-level system must not exceed 5m.
Never short-circuit the busbars. Positive cable = red, negative = black. Reversed polarity causes severe module damage.

images.caption: Master/slave power cable wiring (+/–)
Module stack numbering (up to 10 units)

topics.title: Fault 1 / Fault 2 states – what the binary codes mean
steps: Three alert levels: Warning (module likely to become unstable, clears on recovery), Fault 1 (low-level fault — red indicator flashes, blue indicators show the fault number in binary; may need a corrective action to clear), Fault 2 (high-level fault — red indicator solid on; the module is taken out of use until resolved).

Fault 1 and Fault 2 share the same 11–12 condition codes, just at different severity thresholds: 1) highest cell voltage too high, 2) lowest cell voltage too low, 3) charge current too high, 4) discharge current too high, 5) charge power too high, 6) discharge power too high, 7) battery temperature too high, 8) battery temperature too low, 9) cell voltage difference too large (Fault1) / pack voltage too low (Fault2 #9), 10) module temperature difference too large (Fault1) / BMS hardware fault (Fault2 #10), 11) inter-module communication lost too long. Fault 2 adds #12: communication with the higher-level system lost too long.
Ensure the higher-level system is configured per the diagnosis tables so it limits charge/discharge current in an abnormal state to avoid an escalation to Fault 2.

images.caption: Fault 1 / Fault 2 condition reference grid

topics.title: Abnormality remedies – voltage, current, temperature, comms, SOC
steps: Cell overvoltage (Fault 1): discharge the ESS at ≤ 63A via the higher-level system until the highest cell voltage is < 4.2V, then re-activate once the red indicator turns off.

Cell undervoltage (Fault 1): charge the ESS at ≤ 63A until the lowest cell voltage is > 3V, then re-activate (the ESS recharges 10 minutes before running diagnosis). Note: the module turns itself off 10 minutes after entering Fault 2.
Large voltage difference (lowest cell > 3.5V but spread exceeds tolerance): shut off the higher-level system and wait for cell balancing to complete, then re-activate.
Over-charge / over-discharge current (Fault 1): set the max charge/discharge current to < 63A on the higher-level system, then re-activate.
Over-charge / over-discharge power (residential models EM048063P3S2, EM048126P3S7 only): ensure the higher-level system is configured not to exceed the module's max charge/discharge power.
High battery temperature: check ambient temperature, run air-con until ambient is below 30°C, deactivate the ESS for 2 hours to cool down, then re-activate.
Low battery temperature: check ambient temperature, run air-con/heating until ambient is above 18°C, deactivate the ESS for 2 hours to warm up, then re-activate.
Large internal temperature difference: remove nearby heating/cooling sources, deactivate for ~2 hours until the difference is under 5°C, then re-activate.
Lost communication between modules: deactivate the ESS, check intra-rack comms cables are properly connected, then re-activate.
Lost communication with the higher-level system: deactivate the ESS, check the higher-level comms cable between the master module and the system, then re-activate.
SOC too low: charge at ≤ 63A until SOC ≥ 3%. SOC too high: discharge at ≤ 63A until SOC ≤ 98%.

images.caption: Abnormality remedy reference table (1 of 2)
Abnormality remedy reference table (2 of 2)

topics.title: SolaX warranty ownership — process note
steps: SolaX's consumer warranty is their own business, not ours (currently understood to be 5 years).
Battery modules are a component, not a standalone consumer product — we do not offer a direct consumer warranty on them.
There is a B2B warranty between us and SolaX, with strict data requirements for any claim, but it goes direct to SolaX only — they deal with their own customers.
If SolaX refers one of their customers back to us for a module warranty claim, escalate internally rather than actioning it as our claim — push back firmly to SolaX, gently to the customer.

devices.name: HV Battery Charger (loan unit) & dispatch process
devices.summary: Manual HV battery charging procedure using the LG Chem loan AC/DC charger, plus the internal process for requesting and dispatching a charger.

topics.title: Manual charging procedure (electrically qualified personnel only)
steps: IMPORTANT: never leave charging unattended, and never charge beyond the “Charge to” voltage — exceeding the maximum voltage is a safety risk.
1. Ensure all battery internal breakers/switches are OFF.
2. Remove the battery's top cover (black section), then the secondary cover underneath (socket set required).
3. Measure battery voltage at the fuse positions on top of the battery (multimeter).
4. Connect the AC/DC charger to an AC power point; ensure its output is OFF (Output On/Off button).
5. Select the charger's voltage range: below 120V measured → use the 60–120V range; 120V or above → use the 120–160V range.
6. Remove the battery's Anderson plug from the DC/DC converter; separate the battery Anderson plugs into two cables.
7. Connect the battery Anderson plugs to the charger's Anderson plugs — double-check polarity is correct before proceeding.
8. With the Inline Breaker OFF, press the charger's Output On/Off button, then turn the Inline Breaker ON to begin charging.

9. Charge to the target “Charge to” voltage for the model (allow up to 2 hours from minimum to target). To check voltage without disconnecting, turn the charger output off and wait 1 minute before measuring.
10. Once target voltage is reached, turn the charger Output OFF, then the Inline Breaker OFF.
11. Disconnect the AC cable and the charger/battery Anderson plug connection; reconnect the battery's own Anderson plugs together and back to the DC/DC converter.
12. Refit both battery top covers; the battery can now be turned back on and reconnected to the inverter.
13. Repack the charger and return it to LG Chem.
notes: RESU7H: minimum 60V, charge-to 107V, maximum 124V. RESU10H: minimum 84V, charge-to 150V, maximum 174V.
Starting charge sequence: Charger Output ON → Inline Breaker ON → Battery 2-Pole CB ON. Stopping sequence: Charger Output OFF → Inline Breaker OFF → Battery 2-Pole CB OFF.
If unsure about the process, contact technical support on [contact phone removed].
To check battery SOC before charging, refer to the ‘On + FAULT light’ scenario in the LG HV Battery reference.

images.caption: Loan HV charger connection diagram

topics.title: HV Charger request & dispatch workflow
steps: 1. Installer is onsite.
2. Troubleshoot and confirm a charger is actually required.
3. Raise a ticket and attach evidence (photos/readings).
4. Send the HV Charger Form to the installer and request shipping details.

decisionTree.question: Has the completed HV Charger Form been received?

branches.result: Assign the ticket to KJ, who arranges dispatch and manages the ticket from there.
Follow up with the installer and resend the HV Charger Form if required.

notes: IMPORTANT: keep the ticket in your own name and do NOT assign it to KJ until the completed form has been received.

devices.name: SMA Inverter + LG HV Battery (SBS series)
devices.summary: SMA Sunny Boy Storage (SBS) inverters paired with LG RESU HV batteries (7H/10H/10H-R/10H-C).

topics.title: Communications check – 10-HC
steps: Check the battery's communication cables for GND-AUX and BAT-ENABLE.
Measure CAN_H to CAN_L: 0.5V–1V means the inverter IS communicating with the battery; 0V on the inverter's end means it is NOT.
Measure GND-AUX to BAT-ENABLE: 200mV–400mV means the battery IS communicating; 0V on the battery's end means it is NOT.
notes: For a 10HC system specifically, checking CAN_H/CAN_L alone may not reliably indicate communication status — also ask the installer to log in to the SMA portal to verify the inverter is detecting and communicating with the battery.

images.caption: SMA terminal block assignment — CAN-H / CAN-L

topics.title: All battery lights flashing – corrupted firmware
steps: Isolate the battery, turn the CBs on and observe the lights.
If ALL battery lights flash while isolated, the battery firmware is corrupted.
Ask the installer whether the inverter or its components were replaced, and check with SMA whether firmware was flashed from the inverter.
Turn off the CBs, lift the top cover, remove the inner metal plate, check fuse continuity, then unplug the Anderson plug and measure voltage with the 2-Pole CB ON.

decisionTree.question: What is the measured Anderson Plug voltage?

branches.result: The battery only requires a firmware update. Inform the installer it needs a reflash at the warehouse — arrange shipping at the customer's expense.

topics.title: SBS 2.5 with RESU 7H/10H – Fault 9217
steps: Fault 9217 means the output supply voltage from the battery interface module is too high.
Immediately turn off the DC isolator switch on the inverter.
Measure DC voltage and confirm it's below the inverter's maximum input voltage.

Check the wire connected to position F on each terminal block that links the SBS battery interface module to the batteries — this connection is only required when a backup unit is installed and wired to it.
Removing these wires (where not legitimately required for a backup unit) has been observed to clear Fault 9217.
notes: CAN H and L should be a twisted pair to minimise interference. Four wires are needed for comms: CAN H/L, Enable, and Ground. Use different-coloured Ethernet cable conductors to help trace wiring issues.

images.caption: SBS charging position reference — RESU 7H / RESU 10H

topics.title: PUK code requirement for batteries replaced 2021–2022+
steps: Any battery replaced after 2021 or 2022 requires a Developer PUK code to be uploaded to the SMA inverter (image deletion / reset via PUK code).

topics.title: Accessing the inverter WebUI
steps: Requires an SMA inverter supporting WebUI, and a smart device with Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

Connect directly to the inverter's own Wi-Fi: SSID format is SMA[serial number]. Password is either ‘SMA12345’ or the device-specific WPA2-PSK password on the inverter's type label, depending on firmware/model and commissioning stage.
Open a browser and enter: 192.168.12.3 (direct Wi-Fi), or 169.254.12.3 (direct Ethernet), or the inverter's network-assigned IP (if on the customer's network).
Log in as Installer or User with the password set during commissioning.

images.caption: SMA WebUI — network selection screen
SMA inverter nameplate / WebUI login fields (sensitive fields pre-redacted in source)

topics.title: SMA event code reference (curated)
steps: The full SMA event message list is published by SMA at manuals.sma.de (SBSxx-10 manual). The categories below are the ones most relevant to day-to-day LG HV battery troubleshooting; see the Fault Code Lookup tab for the searchable table of individual codes.

Grid incidents (101–701 series): voltage/frequency out of range, grid disconnected, L/N swapped, grounding missing, phase/neutral not connected — mostly site wiring/grid issues, verify country data set and grid connection before contacting Service.
DC-side faults (3301–3901): unstable operation, DC overvoltage/overcurrent, insulation failure, high leakage current — check battery/DC cabling for ground faults and correct battery selection first.
Internal hardware faults (6001–7002, 8101–9001): mostly “contact the Service” conditions — these are internal inverter electronics, not field-fixable.
Battery system faults (9301–9354): BMS-reported conditions — most resolve by checking DC connection/comms test first, then escalate to the battery manufacturer (LG) if the test passes.
Backup/SPS faults (9202–9223): overvoltage/short circuit/overload in the battery-backup circuit — check load levels and automatic transfer switch wiring first.

devices.name: SolarEdge Inverter + LG HV Battery (StorEdge)
devices.summary: SolarEdge StorEdge inverters paired with LG RESU HV batteries (7H-R/10H-R). Includes the LGESAU fault-code-to-RMA decision guide.

topics.title: Power cycle (SolarEdge-specific steps)
steps: Turn off the toggle switch on the inverter (0 position).
Turn off the PV system: Inverter AC Isolator → PV Array DC Isolator → Battery DC Isolator.
Open the bottom-right battery door, turn OFF the 5-Pole CB then the 2-Pole CB, wait one minute, then turn ON the 2-Pole CB then the 5-Pole CB.
Wait one minute and observe: FAULT light? Shuts down in 15–20s? Stays on?
If it doesn't trip: turn the system back on in order (Battery DC → PV Array DC → Inverter AC → toggle switch to ON), then allow up to 10 minutes to recover.
notes: If FAULT comes on, capture video and send to [contact email removed].

images.caption: Battery disconnect switch (1) and circuit breaker (2) locations
LED reference: Power on / Charging / Discharging / Fault states

topics.title: Meter troubleshooting
steps: If <OK> is not shown on the meter status screen, the meter isn't communicating with the inverter's communication board — check for loose connections and correct RS-485 wiring between the meter's 4-pin terminal block and the StorEdge Interface.
Error 3x6E (or Error 185) – Meter Comm. Error: verify RS-485 cable/connectors and the meter's AC connection.

Power [Wh] Import value not advancing while there's real load consumption: check meter status LEDs are lit (meter has power), check the meter breaker is ON, check the 10-pin AC wiring, and check CT wiring — white CT wire to L1 white, black CT wire to L1 black.
If the green power LEDs are not green (should indicate import direction), the CTs are likely reversed.

images.caption: Meter RS485 wiring connections

topics.title: Battery troubleshooting (StorEdge status screen)
steps: The State line should show Charging, Discharging, Idle, Off, or Init.
Error 3x6B (or Error 186) – Battery Comm. Error: check the RS-485 control connection, and the communication/ID DIP switch settings on the battery.
State shows Idle instead of Charging/Discharging: check the system configuration and the DC connection.
“Battery Internal Fault” displayed: note the Fault # and Modbus ID shown, and refer to the battery documentation / escalate with those details.

images.caption: StorEdge status screen — SOC / power / state readout
LED indicator — troubleshooting action reference

topics.title: RS-485 / battery protocol configuration
steps: Turn the inverter ON/OFF switch to OFF.
Go to Communication → RS485-1 Conf → Device Type → Multi Devices → Battery 1.
Set Device Type → Battery Pack; select protocol → LG Battery; ID → 15.
Use Battery Info to verify the battery's information displays correctly; if not, check the wiring to the battery.
Always have the battery's serial number and firmware version ready before contacting support.

images.caption: RS-485 wiring — ground/neutral reference
Wiring diagram — connecting two LG batteries

topics.title: Firmware upgrade (inverter, via activation card)
steps: Confirm the inverter is activated (activation card used at commissioning), the ON/OFF switch is OFF, AC voltage is OFF, and (if applicable) the StorEdge Interface switch is OFF.
Remove the inverter cover and insert the firmware card into the “CARD” slot on the communication board.
Turn ON the battery AUX switch and circuit breaker; wait 1 minute.
Turn ON AC to the StorEdge Interface, then AC to the inverter — the upgrade starts automatically.
Wait for “Done” on the LCD, then remove the card.
notes: ELECTRICAL SHOCK HAZARD — do not touch uninsulated wires while the cover is removed.

topics.title: Ideal mode on replacement
steps: Confirm the new battery shows only the ON light; access the SolarEdge Monitoring Portal.
Turn the inverter toggle switch to 0, wait 2–3 minutes for it to de-energise, then open the battery door and turn OFF the 5-Pole then 2-Pole CB.
Turn OFF then back ON the Inverter AC Isolator (wait 1 minute), then turn ON the 2-Pole then 5-Pole CB.
Turn the toggle switch back to ON and watch the Monitoring Portal to see if the battery is cycling correctly.
If it still doesn't work: isolate the battery, run an isolation test, and ask SolarEdge to run an optimiser test. If that also fails, escalate to SolarEdge.

topics.title: SolarEdge Fault 43 (DC-DC issue)
steps: Call SolarEdge to get the fault log; check inverter fault logs for Fault 43.
Send logs to [contact email removed].

images.caption: DC-DC converter board — status LED location

topics.title: Error 3X82 / Sleep mode (10HR)
steps: Examine the battery (should show only ON light, or no light). Access the SolarEdge Monitoring Portal.
Turn the inverter toggle switch to 0, wait 2–3 minutes, open the battery door, turn OFF the 5-Pole then 2-Pole CB.
Turn OFF/ON the Inverter AC Isolator, turn ON the 2-Pole then 5-Pole CB. If lights stay on through this isolation, the battery fuse is confirmed intact.
Turn the toggle switch back ON and watch the Monitoring Portal to see if the battery cycles.

decisionTree.question: What do you observe?

branches.result: Check the inverter fuse — a blown inverter fuse can put the battery into sleep mode or trigger a 3X82 error (battery firmware not detected). If firmware is corrupted or 3X82 is present, the inverter portal will show battery firmware as 0.0.0.0.

Ask the installer to contact SolarEdge for further assistance and isolate the battery until resolved. For 10HR batteries, firmware must be reflashed at the warehouse — it cannot be done on site. Confirm who covers the reflash cost (LG, installer, or customer) before proceeding.

topics.title: DC-DC converter fault codes 4 / 6 / 8 – decision tree
steps: Check for fault codes 4, 6, and 8 in the SolarEdge fault log (request SolarEdge send the log for the past 30–90 days and filter out plain battery-communication noise in Excel).

decisionTree.question: Are fault codes present, and how many?

branches.result: Monitor the system — no action needed.
This is a DC-DC converter issue on the battery side — follow the self-approval matrix (see LGESAU guide below).

Confirm with the installer whether there is reverse polarity on site. If no reverse polarity found, capture DC cabling photos: low resistance at the inverter terminals → SolarEdge communication board failure; otherwise isolate the battery and email the fault log, images and serial number/case ID to LGES for escalation.
This points to a DC-DC converter issue requiring SolarEdge (SV) involvement.

notes: Always filter out battery-communication noise and confirm the inverter is otherwise clean, and check DC connections at both battery and inverter, before escalating.

images.caption: DC-DC converter board — component reference

topics.title: LGESAU fault code → RMA decision guide
steps: Purpose: helps the Service & Warranty team identify common battery faults, review prior investigation findings, and decide the right troubleshooting or RMA action. RMA decisions should be based on fault history, system behaviour, logs and LGESAU guidance — investigate further where root cause isn't confirmed.

faultCodeTable.name: AP Voltage High
faultCodeTable.issue: Telemetry shows AP voltage above 175V, sometimes over 200V.
faultCodeTable.action: Review telemetry for abnormal AP voltage, confirm recurrence; if consistent with prior cases, raise RMA. LGESAU investigates/replaces the DCDC converter.

faultCodeTable.name: DC Terminal Overvoltage
faultCodeTable.action: Check telemetry for >500V events, review frequency; if occurring thousands of times, raise RMA. LGESAU investigates the DCDC converter.
faultCodeTable.rmaDecision: Yes – particularly when the fault occurs thousands of times.

faultCodeTable.name: Abnormal Battery Operation
faultCodeTable.issue: Hundreds/thousands of Fault 4 events; battery may not charge/discharge correctly or trips occasionally.
faultCodeTable.action: Check occurrence count, confirm charge/discharge behaviour, review other active fault codes. Raise RMA if thousands of occurrences affect operation.
faultCodeTable.rmaDecision: Yes – when repeated faults affect operation.

faultCodeTable.name: DCDC Communication Error / Link Overvoltage (CB Open)
faultCodeTable.issue: Often appear together with other errors; may not independently affect operation.
faultCodeTable.action: Check if battery operates normally, review other active codes and installation conditions. Arrange battery collection for testing if needed.
faultCodeTable.rmaDecision: Case-by-case – do not raise an RMA on these alone without further assessment.

faultCodeTable.name: Temperature Deviation / Overtemperature Deviation
faultCodeTable.issue: Battery reports a temperature deviation fault.
faultCodeTable.action: Confirm install location/sun exposure, review readings/frequency. Raise RMA if readings look normal but the fault repeats tens/hundreds of times.
faultCodeTable.rmaDecision: Yes – when recurring and supported by logs.

faultCodeTable.name: Cell Imbalance (Overvoltage Fault 2 – CIM)
faultCodeTable.action: Confirm in inverter logs, record details, raise RMA for battery investigation.

faultCodeTable.name: Overcharge Power Limit Fault 2
faultCodeTable.issue: Battery reports an overcharge power limit fault.
faultCodeTable.action: Review fault history/operation, check for other codes, escalate recurring issues to LGESAU; RMA where approved, pending further testing.

faultCodeTable.name: Battery Internal Fault
faultCodeTable.issue: Internal battery fault; note some newer batteries report this due to a firmware issue on version 1.9.6.0.
faultCodeTable.action: Confirm the fault, check firmware version, raise RMA under the existing process. If firmware is 1.9.6.0, arrange assessment and update to 2.0.5.0 at LGESAU.
faultCodeTable.rmaDecision: Yes – RMA required under current process.

faultCodeTable.name: Reverse Polarity
faultCodeTable.issue: Inverter reports reverse polarity; both inverter-side and battery-side causes seen previously.
faultCodeTable.action: Confirm with SolarEdge first and have them investigate the inverter; escalate to LGESAU only if the fault continues after inverter-side investigation.

generalRmaTable.situation: Recurring Fault 3 or 4 with thousands of occurrences
Battery idle due to inverter or meter issue
Suspected battery fuse or DCDC damage

notes: Always review available battery and inverter logs before deciding, except where an approved procedure allows immediate RMA.
Record: fault code, occurrence count, battery serial number, firmware version, and system behaviour.
Confirm whether the fault relates to the battery, inverter, communication, or installation — don't assume root cause just because a replacement battery operates normally.
Cases awaiting LGESAU testing must stay marked “Pending LG Approval”.

Self-approval reference (LGES): normal battery/HV current range is 34.1A–42.1A; the battery self-protects by tripping (Fault 2) above 48.7A. 44A alone is within the no-error band (alarm threshold is above 44.1A).

topics.title: Firmware 2.0.6.0 SolarEdge compatibility
steps: New batteries now ship with firmware 2.0.6.0; SolarEdge has raised compatibility concerns (LG HQ has tested 2.0.5.0/2.0.6.0; SolarEdge testing/packaging support is still pending as of the source document).

decisionTree.question: What's the battery's situation?

branches.result: No action required — let it continue operating.
Ask SolarEdge to attempt a remote firmware update to 1.9.6.0.
Arrange an on-site software update — get cost approval before scheduling the visit.
Consider battery replacement as a last resort — requires LGESAU case-by-case approval.
Ensure both refurbished batteries have matching firmware 2.0.5.0; coordinate with LGESAU before dispatch.

notes: Do NOT replace an operational battery solely because it's running firmware 2.0.6.0.

topics.title: Battery idle / not charging or discharging
steps: Possible causes: inverter fuse issue, battery fuse issue, missing 12V signal from the inverter, inverter meter fault, or inverter malfunction.
Step 1: confirm the battery powers on and shows the ON indicator.
Step 2: if powered on, have the installer check the inverter fuse and operation.
Step 3: if not powered on, arrange a battery fuse check via an authorised technician following the safety procedure.
Step 4: have the installer verify the 12V signal from inverter to battery.
Step 5: confirm the inverter meter is detected and communicating.
notes: Inverter fuse / 12V signal / meter issue → refer to the inverter manufacturer.
Battery fuse issue → contact LGESAU to confirm a replacement fuse can be provided.
Suspected DC-DC converter damage → escalate to LGESAU for assessment and possible replacement.

topics.title: Reading the LG battery log & telemetry export
steps: The exported LG battery Excel file has two sheets: Logs (event/error history) and Telems (operating telemetry). Always review Logs first.
On the Logs sheet: freeze the header row (View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Top Row) and enable filters (Ctrl+Shift+L).
Battery ID column: 15 = Primary Battery, 14 = Secondary Battery — filter by this to isolate which battery logged an event in multi-battery systems.

Filter the Battery Error Code column to find recurring/critical faults, check if multiple codes occurred together, and ignore irrelevant informational events. Start with critical codes before reviewing warnings.
Switch to the Telems sheet, freeze its header row and enable filters the same way. You can hide HvPower, DcPower, ChargeEnergyDelta and DischargeEnergyDelta to reduce clutter.

Key telemetry columns: Date, Battery SN, HvCurrent, HvVoltage, BatteryVoltage, BatteryCurrent, BatteryTemp, BatteryState, ChargedPower, DischargedPower, FullpackEnergyAvail, EnergyRemaining, StoredEnergyLevel (SOC).

To investigate a fault: filter the Telems Date column to the exact fault timestamp from the Logs sheet, review values immediately before/during/after, and check whether they were within normal operating range.
notes: If telemetry stays within normal range at the fault timestamp, the event may be transient or caused by another component. If one or more values move outside their expected range at the same moment, that's strong evidence for root cause.
