sma.sourceNote: Curated from the SMA SBSxx-10 event message manual (full reference: manuals.sma.de/SBSxx-10/en-US/391460235.html). Internal hardware codes that only ever resolve to “contact the Service” are grouped/summarised rather than listed individually.

codes.title: Grid incident – grid voltage/impedance too high
codes.detail: Inverter disconnected from the utility grid.
codes.action: Ensure the correct country data set is configured. Check whether grid voltage at the connection point stays permanently in range. If out of range due to local grid conditions, contact the grid operator; if in range and the message persists, contact the Service.

codes.title: Grid incident – grid disconnected / AC cable damaged / voltage too low
codes.detail: Inverter disconnected from the utility grid.
codes.action: Ensure the miniature circuit breaker is switched on, the AC cable is undamaged and connected correctly, and the country data set is configured correctly. Check grid voltage stays in range; contact the grid operator or Service as above.

codes.title: Grid incident – 10-minute average grid voltage out of range
codes.detail: Grid voltage/impedance too high; inverter disconnects to maintain power quality.
codes.action: Check grid voltage during feed-in; contact the grid operator or Service as above.

codes.title: Active power limit – AC voltage
codes.detail: Inverter reduced power due to high grid voltage.
codes.action: Monitor fluctuation frequency; if frequent, contact the grid operator to request a parameter change, then discuss with Service.

codes.title: Grid incident – stand-alone grid / large frequency change
codes.detail: Inverter disconnected from the grid.
codes.action: Check the grid connection for significant short-term frequency fluctuations.

codes.title: Grid incident – power frequency out of range
codes.detail: Inverter disconnected from the grid.
codes.action: Check frequency fluctuation; contact the grid operator for approval to adjust operating parameters if frequent.

codes.title: Active power limit – AC frequency
codes.detail: Inverter reduced power due to high frequency.
codes.action: Check frequency fluctuation; contact the grid operator for approval if frequent.

codes.title: Grid incident – excess DC current in grid current
codes.detail: Excessively high proportion of DC detected in grid current.
codes.action: Check the grid connection for DC; if frequent, ask the grid operator about raising the monitoring threshold.

codes.title: Frequency not permitted – check parameter
codes.detail: Power frequency out of permissible range.
codes.action: Check frequency fluctuation frequency; contact the grid operator / Service as above.

codes.title: Grounding connection missing
codes.detail: Grounding conductor not correctly connected.
codes.action: Ensure the grounding conductor is correctly connected.

codes.title: L / N swapped
codes.detail: Connection of L and N is swapped.
codes.action: Correct the L/N connection per the installation manual.

codes.title: 2nd phase connected to N
codes.detail: A second line conductor is connected to N.
codes.action: Connect the neutral conductor to N per the installation manual.

codes.title: Phase(s) or neutral conductor not connected
codes.detail: L or N not connected.
codes.action: Ensure L and N are connected, AC conductors undamaged, and the miniature circuit breaker is on.

codes.title: Reconnection fault – grid
codes.detail: Changed country data set or parameter doesn't match local requirements; inverter cannot connect.
codes.action: Ensure the country data set is configured correctly (check ‘Set country standard’ parameter).

codes.title: Unstable operation
codes.detail: Not enough power at the DC input for stable operation; cannot connect to the grid.
codes.action: Ensure the correct battery type is configured.

codes.title: DC overvoltage – disconnect PV array
codes.detail: Overvoltage at the DC input; can destroy the inverter.
codes.action: Immediately disconnect the inverter from all voltage sources. Check DC voltage is below the inverter's max input before reconnecting. Confirm the correct battery is selected. Contact Service if it repeats.

codes.title: Insulation failure – check generator
codes.detail: Ground fault detected on the DC side.
codes.action: Check the battery and DC cabling for ground faults.

codes.title: High leakage current – check PV array
codes.detail: Leakage current too high — ground fault, residual current or malfunction.
codes.action: Check the battery and DC cabling for ground faults. Inverter auto-reconnects once the fault clears.

codes.title: Residual current too high – check PV array
codes.detail: Residual current from brief grounding of the battery or DC cabling.
codes.action: Check the battery and DC cabling for ground faults.

codes.title: DC overcurrent – check PV array
codes.detail: Overcurrent at the DC input; feed-in briefly interrupted.
codes.action: If frequent, ensure the battery is correctly connected and the correct battery is selected.

codes.title: DC power too low / generator voltage too low
codes.action: Check for an inverter/battery firmware update and apply it. If none available, check for other concurrent event messages and action those instead.

codes.title: Internal data/memory faults (system data restored/defective, main/code memory defective, CPU self-test, data inconsistency)
codes.detail: Internal hardware/firmware condition.
codes.action: If the message repeats, contact the Service.

codes.title: Internal processor faults (Execution, Watchdog, General BSP, Version test)
codes.detail: Processor defect.
codes.action: Contact the Service.

codes.title: Measurement errors (DI converter, grid current/voltage sensor offsets)
codes.detail: Measurement error.
codes.action: Contact the Service.

codes.title: Overvoltage grid (HW) / intermediate circuit (HW)
codes.action: Check for a firmware update and apply it; if none available, contact Service.

codes.title: Overcurrent input A / B / C (HW)
codes.action: Check for firmware update; check battery for faults; ensure no short circuit at the DC connection; contact Service if it repeats.

codes.title: UCE monitoring / bridge short-circuit / on-board supply disturbance / power unit / overcurrent battery (HW) / precharge protection
codes.detail: Internal hardware conditions.
codes.action: Contact the Service (check firmware for 6462).

codes.title: Overtemperature – interior / power unit / boost converter
codes.action: Check airflow is free of dirt/obstruction, ambient temperature doesn't exceed spec (typically +45°C), and the inverter isn't in direct sun. Contact Service if it repeats despite that.

codes.title: Minimum operating temperature not reached
codes.detail: Inverter resumes grid feed-in only once temperature reaches − 25°C.
codes.action: Informational — no action needed until temperature rises.

codes.title: Overcurrent grid (SW)
codes.action: Check if other inverters on-site show the same event (grid issue) vs. just this one (contact Service).

codes.title: Overvoltage intermediate circuit (SW)
codes.action: Check for firmware update; check whether a DC overvoltage event preceded it; contact Service.

codes.title: Charge / discharge battery overcurrent (SW limit)
codes.action: Check for firmware update; contact Service if it repeats.

codes.title: Battery undervoltage / overvoltage (SW limit)
codes.action: Check for firmware update; contact Service if it repeats.

codes.title: Program sequence / no system data
codes.action: Check for firmware update; contact Service if it repeats.

codes.title: DC current sensor offset / DC converter string A or B defective
codes.action: Contact the Service if it repeats.

codes.title: Fault sensor – interior / power unit temperature
codes.detail: Measurement error.
codes.action: Contact the Service.

codes.title: Communication fault with meter unit
codes.detail: Inverter not receiving data from the energy meter.
codes.action: Ensure the energy meter is correctly integrated into the same network as the inverter.

codes.title: Communication to backup module disrupted
codes.detail: Comms between inverter and SMA Backup Unit Controller disrupted.
codes.action: Check cable requirements are met, run a communication test; contact the ATS manufacturer or Service based on the result.

codes.title: Communication to battery interface module disrupted
codes.detail: Comms between inverter and battery interface module disrupted.
codes.action: Ensure the ribbon cable is in perfect condition and securely plugged in. Contact the Service if confirmed intact.

codes.title: Grid disconnection point / relay defect
codes.detail: Grid relay of the inverter defective.
codes.action: Contact the Service.

codes.title: 24h relay test
codes.detail: Relay test failed.
codes.action: Contact the Service if it repeats.

codes.title: Active power limit – temperature
codes.detail: Power output reduced >10 minutes due to excessive temperature.
codes.action: Clean cooling fins/air ducts, ensure sufficient ventilation, ambient under +45°C, and no direct solar irradiation on the unit.

codes.title: SPS AC overvoltage / short circuit in SPS outlet
codes.detail: AC source connected to the secure-power-supply outlet, or load exceeds max permissible current.
codes.action: Check/correct the SPS slot connection, or reduce the load / use a lower-inrush appliance.

codes.title: AC overvoltage backup (fast/slow)
codes.detail: Backup-grid voltage too high or load steps too large.
codes.action: Check for firmware update; contact Service if none available.

codes.title: Short circuit in backup
codes.detail: Loads in the battery-backup grid too high.
codes.action: Reduce loads; contact the Service.

codes.title: Backup module bimetal switch / relay error / N-PE monitoring / overtemperature
codes.detail: Automatic transfer switching device error.
codes.action: Contact the manufacturer of the automatic transfer switching device.

codes.title: Black start battery voltage too low
codes.detail: Backup battery's service life has expired.
codes.action: Procure and exchange a new backup battery; contact the Service.

codes.title: Battery interface module hardware/communication errors
codes.detail: Various BIM-side faults.
codes.action: Check the ribbon cable / plug connections to battery and ATS; run a communication test; contact Service if it repeats.

codes.title: New battery detected / service life expiring / connection fault / unauthorized system / voltage deviation / battery system defective / communication error
codes.detail: Various BMS-reported conditions.
codes.action: Check DC connection and run a communication test first; if the test passes, contact the battery manufacturer (LG); if it fails, contact the Service.

codes.title: Battery cell over/undervoltage, low/overtemperature, imbalance, internal HW fault
codes.detail: Cell-level or internal battery faults.
codes.action: Contact the battery manufacturer (LG).

codes.title: Battery charging/start issues, incorrect disconnection switch position, short circuit, thermal management failure, heating procedure unsuccessful
codes.detail: Various BMS conditions.
codes.action: Check for firmware update; contact the battery manufacturer if it persists.

codes.detail: Hundreds/thousands of Fault 4 events; battery may not charge/discharge correctly or trips occasionally.
codes.action: Check occurrence count, confirm charge/discharge behaviour, review other active fault codes. Raise RMA if thousands of occurrences affect operation. RMA decision: Yes – when repeated faults affect operation. Likely component: DCDC converter or battery cells

codes.title: DCDC Communication Error / Link Overvoltage (CB Open)
codes.detail: Often appear together with other errors; may not independently affect operation.
codes.action: Check if battery operates normally, review other active codes and installation conditions. Arrange battery collection for testing if needed. RMA decision: Case-by-case – do not raise an RMA on these alone without further assessment.

codes.detail: Battery reports a temperature deviation fault.

codes.detail: Battery reports an overcharge power limit fault.
codes.action: Review fault history/operation, check for other codes, escalate recurring issues to LGESAU; RMA where approved, pending further testing. RMA decision: Case-by-case – further investigation required. Likely component: Not yet confirmed

codes.title: Battery Internal Fault
codes.detail: Internal battery fault; note some newer batteries report this due to a firmware issue on version 1.9.6.0.
codes.action: Confirm the fault, check firmware version, raise RMA under the existing process. If firmware is 1.9.6.0, arrange assessment and update to 2.0.5.0 at LGESAU. RMA decision: Yes – RMA required under current process. Likely component: Internal battery fault or firmware

codes.title: Reverse Polarity
codes.detail: Inverter reports reverse polarity; both inverter-side and battery-side causes seen previously.
codes.action: Confirm with SolarEdge first and have them investigate the inverter; escalate to LGESAU only if the fault continues after inverter-side investigation. RMA decision: Case-by-case – investigate the inverter first. Likely component: Inverter or battery

codes.title: BMS Comm Failure
codes.detail: Fault: the lithium battery and inverter cannot communicate.
codes.action: 1. Confirm BMS comms cable sequence matches the install manual and the connection tests normal (CAN or RS-485 per battery mode). 2. Confirm the battery model selected in PV Master matches reality. 3. If ET + BYD HV battery: confirm the battery is connected to its own Wi-Fi and configured for cell count / inverter manufacturer / protocol (requires BYD firmware ≥ V3.012R). 4. Measure the battery's output voltage at the inverter side with a multimeter; confirm polarity. 5. (ET only) Confirm battery power cable polarity is not reversed — ET has polarity protection for HV batteries but not for LV b

codes.title: Meter Comm Failure
codes.detail: Fault: the meter and inverter cannot communicate.
codes.action: 1. Confirm the meter comms cable sequence matches the install manual. 2. If unplugging the BMS comms cable restores meter comms, the BMS cable needs modification (only CAN-H/CAN-L should remain). 3. Confirm the meter model matches the inverter — replace with the GoodWe smart meter if an Ancrel three-phase meter (DTSD1352) is fitted. 4. (Alpha-ESS only) Confirm active vs passive inverter version as above. 5. If the meter itself is suspected faulty, replace it. 6. If all checks pass, contact the GoodWe service team — likely an inverter-side meter communication port issue.

codes.title: Abnormal Battery Charging
codes.detail: Fault: the battery fails to charge, or doesn't charge at normal power.
codes.action: 1. Check BMS fault code — handle per BMS Comm Failure solutions if abnormal. 2. Check PV Master advanced settings for a charging current upper limit. 3. Lead-acid batteries: check capacity setting — charging current = battery capacity × 0.15. 4. Check BMS charging current limit via PV Master monitoring data — this is expected behaviour, explain to the customer, no action needed. 5. Check SOC and BMS charge-overvoltage alarm — if the battery is simply full, explain to the customer, no action needed. 6. Check meter communication status — handle per Meter Comm Failure if abnormal. 7. Confirm the

codes.title: Abnormal Battery Discharging
codes.detail: Fault: the battery fails to discharge, or doesn't discharge at normal power. Follow the same step pattern as Abnormal Battery Charging (BMS fault code, PV Master discharge current limits, battery capacity setting, SOC/undervoltage alarm, meter comms, work mode, safety curve), escalating to GoodWe service if none resolve it.

codes.code: Inverter LED is off – cannot power on
codes.title: Inverter LED is off – cannot power on
codes.detail: 1. Check the inverter DC switch is ON.
codes.action: 2. If connected to PV only: measure open-circuit string voltage. It must reach the inverter's minimum starting voltage; if it does and the inverter still won't start after 5–10 minutes, continue. 3. Check for reverse polarity on any DC string with a multimeter (red lead to positive, black to negative) — rectify on site if found. 4. If connected to battery only: the battery voltage must be above a minimum threshold for the inverter to start. 5. If connected to AC only: measure voltage at the on-grid terminal. If no voltage, check/rectify the on-grid cabling. If voltage is present and it still w

codes.title: DC Injection High | Error 29
codes.detail: Fault: DC injection from the inverter is too high during output.
codes.action: South Africa and Italy have strict DC injection requirements that may need remote parameter adjustment. Upgrade to the latest DSP firmware* (requires GoodWe engineer approval). If the error persists after upgrading, contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: Relay Check | Error 29
codes.detail: Fault: the inverter detected a relay fault.
codes.action: 1. Power off AC & DC, measure voltage between neutral and ground at the on-grid side — should be ≤ 10V; if higher, grounding is poor and needs correcting. 2. Measure resistance between neutral and ground at the backup side — should be < 10Ω. 3. Restart the inverter — if it starts normally, the error was AC-voltage disturbance (no action needed). If it still won't start, contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: Reconnecting / self-test loop
codes.detail: Fault: the auto self-test fails and keeps looping.
codes.action: 1. Confirm the inverter's selected safety regulations match local grid requirements. 2. Confirm each PV string reaches the inverter's minimum starting voltage (check via PV Master). 3. Measure N-to-ground voltage at both the on-grid and backup sides — should be < 10V (poor grounding if ≥ 10V). 4. Pull the AC cable outward to confirm it's well-terminated. 5. Check the specific warning code shown and contact the GoodWe service team with that code if unresolved.

codes.title: Waiting for Power Generation
codes.detail: Fault: PV voltage has reached starting voltage, but the inverter isn't generating power.
codes.action: 1. Confirm the inverter is connected to at least two power sources (PV, battery, AC) — a storage inverter needs at least two to connect to grid. 2. Confirm selected safety regulations match local grid requirements. 3. Confirm each string reaches minimum starting voltage. 4. Check the specific warning code on PV Master and contact GoodWe with that code if needed. 5. For Australia (DRED) or EU (remote shutdown): confirm the required terminal/resistor is fitted (15kΩ DRED resistor for Australian inverters) — contact GoodWe if missing.

codes.title: Terminal Burnt (AC or DC)
codes.detail: Work through each check in order — several outcomes affect warranty status:
codes.action: 1. Was a non-standard (non-GoodWe) DC connector used? If yes → warranty void. 2. Were DC terminals crimped to the user manual's requirements? If not → warranty void. 3. Reverse polarity on any DC string that caused the burn? If yes → site must be rectified; warranty void for that cause. 4. Cross-wiring between DC strings? If found, rectify on site. 5. Poor AC terminal crimping? If yes → warranty void. 6/7. AC cable material/diameter not meeting the manual's requirements (e.g. aluminium without copper-aluminium terminals, or undersized cable)? If so → warranty void. 8. Open the inverter and che

codes.title: Water inside the inverter
codes.detail: 1. Check all used terminals are connected and tight, unused terminals are blocked, and external sealing screws are tight. If sealing is poor, this is an installation defect (not to manual spec) — warranty void.
codes.action: 2. Open the cover and check for stagnant water inside. If present, contact the GoodWe service team. 3. Check for condensation. If it's affecting function, contact GoodWe; if it's not affecting function, it can usually clear itself in good weather.

codes.title: Utility Loss | Error 23
codes.detail: Fault: inverter detects no AC voltage / voltage below the safety threshold.
codes.action: 1. Confirm other equipment on the same grid connection works normally — if not, it's a grid/mains issue; contact an electrician or the grid company. 2. Check the inverter's upper AC switch is closed and not damaged (compare voltage above/below the switch). 3. Check AC wiring/termination by gently pulling the cable. 4. Check the over/under-voltage protector isn't tripped or wired backwards (its upper end must connect to the grid). 5. With AC and DC shut down, measure impedance between live and neutral — should be > 200kΩ (much lower suggests internal continuity — contact GoodWe HQ). 6. Measure

codes.title: Low Generation
codes.detail: 1. Check anti-reverse / over-frequency load reduction / PU curve / slope loading functions aren't unnecessarily limiting output — disable per local requirements if so.
codes.action: 2. Measure grid voltage/frequency — if close to the safety regulation's upper limit, it may be triggering derating; try switching the safety regulation to 50/60Hz Default. 3. Test string open-circuit voltage/short-circuit current against the module's label spec — mismatch suggests a module-side problem. 4. Check installation environment: shading, PV array tilt/azimuth, dirt/debris on panels, hot spots/cracks in modules, or an enclosed (overheating) inverter location. 5. Turn on high-power appliances at midday and watch whether inverter output increases — if not, the power-distribution cabinet'

codes.title: ISO Failure (insulation resistance)
codes.detail: Fault: suspected component problem — insulation resistance to ground is < 100kΩ.
codes.action: 1. Confirm module type (crystalline silicon vs thin film) — thin film needs GoodWe confirmation. 2. Check grounding resistance between module frame and metal bracket — should be ≤ 10Ω. 3. Connect one string at a time to isolate which string (if any) causes the fault — if it only occurs with ALL strings connected, or on specific strings, contact GoodWe to confirm. 4. Measure cable-to-ground impedance per string — should be ≥ 10Ω (cable insulation); for HV battery power line to ground, should be ≥ 1MΩ (500kΩ minimum after repair). 5. Visually inspect module cable surface for damage. 6. Check AC-

codes.title: Ground I | Error 22 / 32 (leakage current)
codes.detail: Fault: detected leakage current is large.
codes.action: 1. If the fault only appears in rainy weather or morning/evening, it's likely high-humidity parasitic capacitance — self-clears on a sunny day. 2. On a sunny day: check DC (module/bracket, should be ≤ 10Ω) and AC (ground wire to grid-tie copper bar, should be ≤ 10Ω) grounding. 3. Plug/unplug each string in turn to isolate a faulty string. 4. For HV battery systems, measure impedance of the HV battery power line to ground — should be ≥ 1Ω. 5. Disconnect the battery (leave only PV + grid) — if it connects to grid normally, the battery cable insulation is the problem; check/correct it.

codes.title: VAC Failure (grid overvoltage)
codes.detail: Fault: grid voltage exceeded the inverter's safety requirement. Follow a similar check sequence to Utility Loss: grid condition, AC switch/wiring, grounding, then escalate to GoodWe if unresolved.

codes.title: Grid Frequency fault
codes.detail: Fault: grid frequency exceeds the range permitted by the inverter's safety regulations. Confirm the correct safety regulation/country set, check for genuine grid frequency fluctuation, and escalate to GoodWe if the condition is not a real grid event.

codes.title: DC Overvoltage (low-voltage battery hybrid)
codes.detail: Fault: DC string input voltage exceeds the inverter's allowable range (LV-battery hybrid inverters).
codes.action: 1. Power off and disconnect all PV strings; measure open-circuit voltage of each string and calculate the maximum expected Voc for the actual configuration and local climate. If max Voc exceeds the inverter's DC voltage range, reduce the panel count per string. 2. Compare PV-side voltage (multimeter) to the value shown on PV Master — mismatch means a sampling/calibration issue (needs calibration tool, or a control board replacement on ES models) — escalate to GoodWe if unresolved.

codes.title: DC Overvoltage (high-voltage battery hybrid)
codes.detail: Fault: DC string input voltage exceeds the inverter's allowable range (HV-battery hybrid inverters, e.g. ET).
codes.action: 1. As above — check string Voc vs the inverter's max DC range; reduce panel count if exceeded. 2. Compare PV-side voltage reading to PV Master's displayed value — calibrate or replace control board (ET only) if mismatched. 3. Check battery voltage against the inverter's DC voltage range — reduce the number of batteries, or contact the battery vendor, if exceeded. 4. Compare battery-side voltage to PV Master's displayed value — calibrate, replace control board, or contact GoodWe if still mismatched.

codes.title: Over Temperature
codes.detail: 1. Confirm installation location meets the user manual's clearance/ventilation requirements — reinstall correctly if not.
codes.action: 2. Measure ambient temperature around the inverter — if over 45°C, cool the environment. 3. If ambient is under 45°C, power off for 15 minutes then restart — if it then runs normally, it was a temporary high-temperature event; if it still fails, contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: EEP ROM read/write failure
codes.detail: Fault: control board storage chip read/write failure. If the inverter runs normally after a restart, no further action is required; otherwise contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: DC Bus voltage too high
codes.detail: Fault: internal DC bus voltage inside the device is too high. This is largely an internal hardware condition — confirm it isn't tied to a DC overvoltage event upstream, otherwise contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: AC output current sensor failure
codes.detail: Internal hardware fault — contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: Control board malfunction (indicator abnormal)
codes.detail: The control board is malfunctioning, causing an indicator to behave abnormally. This is an internal hardware fault — contact the GoodWe service team.

codes.title: Internal inductance noise
codes.detail: 1. Confirm the selected safety regulation matches local grid requirements (mismatches can cause audible switching noise).
codes.action: 2. Measure the actual noise on site with a decibel meter or smartphone app and record video/audio.

codes.title: Backup not working
codes.detail: 1. Verify a common neutral cable is present between the grid and backup circuit.
codes.action: 2. Confirm sufficient grid-side voltage at the inverter (200V–240V is acceptable). 3. Get screenshots of recent performance in the LGES Monitoring app (production, consumption, battery SOC, battery cycling). 4. Confirm the backup function was switched ON at commissioning (PV Master app, iOS/Android, or the GoodWe IoT platform). 5. If still unresolved: re-check the common neutral cable, measure grid-side voltage (200–240V), simulate a blackout (turn off main grid supply and PV), then measure voltage at the inverter's backup output and photograph the reading.

codes.title: Relay Check Failure → RMA
codes.detail: 1. Get the inverter serial number.
codes.action: 2. On the monitoring platform, go to Alarms, re-enter the serial number, and set the alarm status filter to “All” (active + historical). 3. Look for any “Relay Failure” alarm entries and note how often they recur.

codes.title: Dead Short test
codes.detail: Turn off the inverter. The next steps must be completed within 5 minutes of shutdown.
codes.action: Disconnect the battery DC cables on the inverter side. Measure resistance across the inverter's battery terminals. Confirm battery polarity was not reversed. Request photos from the installer (showing the inverter switched off/isolated, resistance reading, serial number sticker, and installation) and email them to [contact email removed].

em048.system: EM048 stacked battery – Fault 1 / Fault 2 condition codes
em048.sourceNote: Binary fault-number codes shown on the blue indicator LEDs. Fault 1 = red indicator flashing (low-level, may clear itself with a corrective action). Fault 2 = red indicator solid on (high-level, module taken out of use).

codes.title: Highest cell voltage too high
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Early overvoltage warning — BMS may slow charging or balance cells.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Cell voltage exceeded the safe level — risk of electrolyte breakdown/swelling; BMS triggers a protective fault.

codes.title: Lowest cell voltage too low
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Minor under-voltage/imbalance — BMS alerts or limits discharge.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Cell dropped below the safe discharge limit — BMS stops discharge.

codes.title: Charge current too high
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Slightly above allowed charging current — BMS may auto-reduce rate.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Charging current too high — risk of overheat/damage; BMS faults to prevent overcharge stress.

codes.title: Discharge current too high
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Discharge current above normal safe range — BMS may limit output.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Excess discharge current — BMS cuts off output to prevent damage.

codes.title: Charge power too high
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Charging power above rated limit — system slows charging / balances.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Over-power charging condition — BMS stops charging.

codes.title: Discharge power too high
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Discharge power above recommended limit — risk of heating/efficiency loss.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Total discharge power too high — BMS stops or limits output.

codes.title: Battery temperature too high
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Slightly above safe range, often during heavy charge/discharge — BMS cools or limits current.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Exceeded max temperature limit — BMS stops operation.

codes.title: Battery temperature too low
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Below minimum operating temperature — BMS pauses charge/discharge.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Too cold — risk of lithium plating / permanent cell damage; BMS halts until safe temperature is reached.

codes.title: Cell voltage difference too large (Fault 1) / Battery voltage below tolerance (Fault 2)
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Imbalance or ageing cells — BMS attempts cell balancing.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Overall pack voltage below minimum safe threshold — deep discharge/imbalance; BMS disables output.

codes.title: Module temperature difference too large (Fault 1) / BMS hardware fault (Fault 2)
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Uneven cooling/sensor issue inside the module — BMS may limit current and log it.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): BMS internal hardware error — stops battery operation (safety controller fault).

codes.title: Communication with other battery modules lost
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): Temporary inter-module comms loss — system retries.
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Comms loss persisted beyond tolerance — module isolated for safety.

codes.title: Communication with the higher-level system lost (Fault 2 only)
codes.detail: Fault 1 (flashing red): —
codes.action: Fault 2 (solid red): Link to inverter/EMS/gateway broken beyond tolerance — battery goes to safe/standby mode.

hv-batt-symptom.question: What's the symptom on the LG HV Battery?

hv-no-lights.title: No lights — blown fuse or sleep mode
hv-no-lights.summary: Two likely causes: a blown fuse, or the battery is in sleep mode.
steps: Isolate: inverter off, battery disconnected from inverter, CB & AUX switch OFF.
Remove covers and inner metal plate, then check fuse continuity with a multimeter.
If the fuse is blown: request LGES/SSG send two replacement fuses, collect the customer's shipping details.
If the fuse is fine but there's still no light after a power cycle: likely sleep mode. Run an isolation test, and ask SolarEdge to wake the battery by changing its profile.
seeAlso: lg-hv-battery/Battery shows no lights at all

hv-fault-light.question: Have you measured the Anderson Plug voltage yet?

options.label: Yes, I have a voltage reading

res-hv-fault-light-procedure.title: Measuring Anderson Plug voltage
res-hv-fault-light-procedure.summary: Isolate the battery (inverter off, CB/AUX off), remove the covers and inner metal plate, check fuse continuity, then with the 2-Pole CB ON and 5-Pole CB OFF measure voltage at the Anderson Plug.
steps: Once you have a reading, come back and select the matching voltage range.

options.label: 130V or more, but it still trips when isolated

res-hv-under-80.title: Under 80V → Issue RMA
res-hv-under-80.summary: Voltage below 80V on the Anderson Plug.
steps: Issue the RMA.

Investigate root cause: was the inverter replaced? Any rectification work? Any event that caused the SOC to drop (misconfiguration, maintenance work, prolonged load without charging, high load demand, loose/faulty connections)?

res-hv-80-130.title: 80V–130V → Charger form, or try force charge
res-hv-80-130.summary: 80–120V: send a charger form, then dispatch a charger once approved. 120–130V specifically: ask SolarEdge/inverter vendor to try a force charge first.
steps: 80–120V: raise the HV Charger Form (see the HV Charger process).
120–130V: ask SolarEdge whether they can force-charge the battery; if they cannot, request a charger instead.

res-hv-over-130-trips.title: ≥130V but still trips → Issue RMA
res-hv-over-130-trips.summary: Voltage is OK, so voltage is not the cause — this points to an internal battery fault.
steps: Issue an RMA and capture photos/video of the battery tripping for the submission.
Email evidence to [contact email removed].

hv-blinking-on.title: Blinking ON light — possible corrupted firmware
hv-blinking-on.summary: Isolate the battery, cycle the CBs, and watch whether ALL lights flash together.
steps: If all lights flash while isolated → firmware is corrupted.
Ask the installer whether the inverter/components were replaced, and check with the inverter manufacturer whether firmware was flashed from their side.
Measure Anderson Plug voltage: if it's over 135V, only a firmware update is needed — arrange a warehouse reflash (customer-funded freight).

hv-swelling.title: Swelling — photograph and measure
hv-swelling.summary: Photograph the battery (full + zoomed lower-half), serial number, and overall setup/clearances. Send to [contact email removed].
steps: > 5mm: ask the installer to switch the battery OFF, then issue RMA.
< 3mm: leave the battery ON, then issue RMA.
Note: a separate source notes ‘2mm’ as the RMA trigger for LV batteries — when borderline, treat 2mm as the conservative cutoff and confirm with the LG team.
hv-swelling.warning: Always document swelling with photos before lodging the claim.

lv-cb-trip.question: Is this a NEW installation (commissioning) or an OLD/existing one that was working before?

res-lv-cb-new.title: New install — check DIP switches, comms wiring, polarity
res-lv-cb-new.summary: Set DIP switches to match the number of batteries, check the RJ45 comms slot location, and inspect for polarity/wiring issues.
steps: Inspect: DC polarity, communication wiring, short circuits, reverse polarity, external equipment faults, incorrect inverter fuse rating.
SolaX inverter pins 1 & 2; Sungrow inverter pins 4 & 5. Replace the RJ45 cable if required.
If all checks pass, proceed with the RMA.
seeAlso: lg-lv-battery/CB tripping or no communication – decision tree

lv-cb-old-voltage.question: What is the measured DC voltage?

res-lv-cb-old-45plus.title: ≥45V — isolate and re-test trip time
res-lv-cb-old-45plus.summary: Isolate the battery then turn it back on.
steps: If it trips within 5 seconds → faulty battery → issue RMA.
If it does NOT trip quickly, voltage is OK — look at other causes (DIP switches, communication wiring).

res-lv-force-charge-maybe.title: 42–45V — force charge may be possible
res-lv-force-charge-maybe.summary: SOC is effectively at minimum; a force charge may bring it back.
steps: Attempt a force charge via the inverter/vendor.
If force charge is not possible, treat as faulty → issue RMA.

res-lv-faulty-under-42.title: Under 42V — faulty battery
res-lv-faulty-under-42.summary: Force charge is not possible at this voltage.
steps: Issue RMA.

prime-symptom.question: What's the symptom on the LG Prime battery?

options.label: Not sure / just want the basic reset

res-prime-noise.title: High-pitched noise — firmware update
res-prime-noise.summary: Usually resolved via a battery firmware update through Enblock Manager.
steps: Without login: Enblock Manager → login page → “Battery FW Update” → select region → download → scan battery QR (prefix EH257064P8S or EH153064P8S) → follow the update flow.
With login: “Direct Connection Battery” → “Battery Status” → connect → run FW update from the registered system list.

res-prime-3x82.title: Error 3X82 — firmware mismatch after replacement
res-prime-3x82.summary: Caused by a firmware mismatch or missing firmware after swapping the battery.
steps: If never commissioned: complete full commissioning in Enblock Manager.
If replacing an old registered battery: use Maintenance → Replacement.
Commissioning auto-applies the latest firmware (RMD 4.2.1, BMS 2.6.3.4, DCDC 1.4.0.0), which clears the mismatch.
If it persists, recheck the FW update logs or contact LG technical support.

res-prime-fuse.title: Suspected blown fuse — resistance test
res-prime-fuse.summary: Measure fuse resistance with a multimeter (expected 0.2 ± 0.1 Ω).
steps: If normal, reassemble in reverse order — not a fuse issue.
If blown, the ENTIRE battery must be replaced (not just the fuse).

res-prime-leakage.title: Not charging/discharging — check for voltage leakage
res-prime-leakage.summary: Isolate the battery for 5 minutes, then measure DC voltage across the terminals with everything off.
steps: < 10V → fine, no action.
> 10V → leakage confirmed → issue RMA.
Borderline/slightly under 10V → check with the LGES team.

goodwe-symptom.question: What's the symptom on the LGES 5048 inverter?

options.label: Inverter LED off / won't power on
Backup power not working during an outage
Suspect a dead short / considering an RMA
Something else (terminal burnt, water ingress, noise, over-temp, low generation...)

res-goodwe-wifi.title: Wi-Fi / connectivity troubleshooting
res-goodwe-wifi.summary: Check the inverter's Wi-Fi LED, power cycle, and try reseating/reloading the dongle.
steps: See the full Wi-Fi decision tree (can't find SSID / can't connect / LED blink codes / portal offline) in the Device Reference Library → LGES 5048 inverter.

res-goodwe-bms.title: BMS Comm Failure
steps: Check comms cable sequence (CAN or RS-485) against the install manual.
Confirm the battery model selected in PV Master matches the real battery.
Measure output voltage/polarity with a multimeter at the inverter side.
If all checks pass, contact the GoodWe service team — likely the inverter's BMS comm port.

res-goodwe-meter.title: Meter Comm Failure
res-goodwe-meter.summary: The meter and inverter cannot communicate.
steps: Confirm the meter comms cable sequence matches the manual.
Unplug the BMS comms cable temporarily — if meter comms recover, the BMS cable needs rewiring (CAN-H/CAN-L only).
Confirm the correct meter model is fitted.
If unresolved, contact the GoodWe service team.

goodwe-charge-discharge.question: Is it a charging or discharging problem?

res-goodwe-abn-charge.title: Abnormal battery charging
res-goodwe-abn-charge.summary: Multiple possible causes — work through them in order.
steps: Check BMS fault code, PV Master charging current limit, battery capacity setting, SOC/overvoltage alarm, meter comms, work mode (Economic Mode schedule), safety curve, and PV voltage.
If all 9 checks pass, contact the GoodWe service team.

res-goodwe-abn-discharge.title: Abnormal battery discharging
steps: Work through BMS fault code, PV Master limits, capacity setting, SOC, meter comms, work mode and safety curve.
Escalate to GoodWe service if none resolve it.

res-goodwe-no-power.title: Inverter LED off / won't power on
res-goodwe-no-power.summary: Work through DC switch, string voltage, polarity, battery voltage, and AC voltage checks in order.
steps: Confirm the DC switch is ON.
Measure string open-circuit voltage — must exceed minimum starting voltage.
Check for reverse polarity on any DC string.
If battery-only, confirm battery voltage is above the minimum threshold.
If AC-only, measure on-grid terminal voltage; if present and it still won't start, contact GoodWe.
seeAlso: lges-5048/Inverter LED is off – cannot power on

res-goodwe-backup.title: Backup power not working
res-goodwe-backup.summary: Check neutral cabling, grid-side voltage, app settings, and run a blackout simulation if needed.
steps: Verify common neutral cable between grid and backup circuit.
Confirm grid-side voltage is 200–240V at the inverter.
Confirm backup was enabled at commissioning (PV Master or GoodWe IoT).
Simulate a blackout and measure backup output voltage; watch for overload cutouts if the load exceeds backup capacity.

res-goodwe-dead-short.title: Dead short test before RMA
res-goodwe-dead-short.summary: With the inverter off and battery DC cables disconnected (within 5 minutes), measure resistance at the inverter's battery terminals.
steps: 0–10kΩ → dead short confirmed → raise RMA, escalate with GoodWe for a replacement inverter.
> 10kΩ → normal, no dead short.
res-goodwe-dead-short.warning: Confirm battery polarity was not reversed before raising the RMA.

res-goodwe-seelibrary.title: See the full LGES 5048 fault list
res-goodwe-seelibrary.summary: There are 24 documented fault categories for this inverter (terminal burnt, water ingress, ISO failure, grid overvoltage/frequency, DC overvoltage, over-temperature, internal hardware faults, noise, and more).
steps: Open the Device Reference Library → LGES 5048 inverter, or use the Fault Code Lookup tab to search by symptom.

Fault number showing on blue indicators

res-em048-bms.title: SolaX BMS not detected
res-em048-bms.summary: Usually a pin-mapping or cabling issue between the LG battery and SK-SU/BMU.
steps: Identify External vs Internal BMS communication type and check the correct pin mapping (see Device Reference Library → EM048 for the full pin tables).
Verify and rectify cabling for stable communication, then reconnect and power back up in order (battery → panels → inverter).

res-em048-green.title: Green indicator won't turn on
res-em048-green.summary: Likely over-discharged module or a faulty On/Off button.
steps: Measure voltage at the terminal block (remove the power terminal compartment cover first).
If under 42V → do not use this module — replace it.

res-em048-blue-flash.title: Blue indicators flashing — mixed battery models
res-em048-blue-flash.summary: An ESS must use all the same module model.
steps: Remove all comms cables to isolate modules, then identify each module's model number via the On/Off button binary code (hold 5+ seconds).

res-em048-fault-number.title: Fault number on the blue indicators (binary)
res-em048-fault-number.summary: Use the Fault Code Lookup tab (EM048 system) to decode the specific number, or check Fault Number 12 if it's a comms configuration issue.
steps: Fault 1 (red flashing) is a low-level condition that may self-clear with a corrective action (see EM048 ‘Abnormality remedies’ topic for exact current/voltage targets).
Fault 2 (red solid) takes the module out of service until resolved.
seeAlso: em048/Fault 1 / Fault 2 states – what the binary codes mean
em048/Abnormality remedies – voltage, current, temperature, comms, SOC

res-em048-imbalance.title: Voltage imbalance after reset
res-em048-imbalance.summary: If the imbalance persists after a full isolate-and-reset cycle, this is a hardware fault.
steps: Isolate, reset, and power back up; observe LEDs.
If imbalance persists → battery is faulty, replace under warranty. With multiple modules, isolate just the affected one and recommission the rest.

res-em048-reset.title: Reset / reinitialise procedure
steps: Switch off inverter, panel and battery isolators.
Remove comms and DC cables from the battery.
Hold the On/Off button on the master module 5+ seconds until all lights turn off (reinitiated).
Reconnect cables and power back up in order.

res-hv-power-cycle.title: Basic HV battery power cycle
res-hv-power-cycle.summary: Standard first step for most HV battery symptoms.
steps: Turn off Inverter AC → PV Array DC → Battery DC isolators.
Cycle the 5-Pole CB and 2-Pole CB off, wait 1 minute, then back on.
Watch for FAULT light / early trip / staying on.
If it trips, capture video for [contact email removed]. If not, restore the system in reverse order.

res-lv-power-cycle.title: Basic LV battery power cycle
res-lv-power-cycle.summary: Standard first step for most LV battery symptoms.
steps: Turn off Inverter AC → PV Array DC → Battery DC isolators.
Remove the top cover, cycle the circuit breaker off/on with a 1-minute wait.
RESU 3.2EX/6.4EX: customer can do this themselves. RESU 6.5/10/12/13: do not remove the top cover — licensed electrician only if deeper access is needed.

res-prime-power-cycle.title: Basic LG Prime power cycle
steps: Turn off Inverter AC → PV Array DC → Battery DC isolators.
Open the top door, cycle the circuit breaker off/on with a 1-minute wait, observe lights.

res-hv-repeated-fuse.title: Repeated blown fuses — deeper investigation
res-hv-repeated-fuse.summary: This points to a system-level issue, not just a bad fuse.
steps: Inspect the inverter for a blown DC fuse / overheating or loose terminals.
Check inverter fault/error history for DC overcurrent, ground faults, comms failures.
Review site history for repeat battery replacements.
Verify system configuration and comms cabling/termination.
Electrical test: GND-AUX/BAT-ENABLE and RS485H/L should read 200–400mV; CAN_H/L and EN_H/G should read 8–12V.
Check for recent electrical work, grid instability, lightning/surge events or water ingress.
Escalate with full test results, photos, serials and a timeline if still unresolved.

res-sma-all-flashing.title: All lights flashing (SMA) — corrupted firmware
res-sma-all-flashing.summary: Isolate and cycle the CBs; if ALL lights flash, firmware is corrupted.
steps: Ask the installer if the inverter/components were replaced; check with SMA whether firmware was flashed.
Measure Anderson Plug voltage: if > 135V, only a firmware update/reflash at the warehouse is needed (customer-funded freight).
seeAlso: sma-inverter/All battery lights flashing – corrupted firmware

res-sma-comms.title: SMA communication check
res-sma-comms.summary: Measure CAN_H/CAN_L and GND-AUX/BAT-ENABLE (10-HC) or EN_H/EN_G and RS485H/L (10-HR).
steps: 10-HC: CAN_H to CAN_L should read 0.5–1V; GND-AUX to BAT-ENABLE should read 200–400mV.
10-HR: EN_H to EN_G should read 8–12V; RS485H to RS485L should read 400mV–1V.
0V on either end means that side isn't communicating — check cabling/connectors.

res-solaredge-comms.title: SolarEdge communication check
res-solaredge-comms.summary: Check the battery status screen and relevant error code.
steps: Error 3x6B / 186 (Battery Comm Error): check the RS-485 control connection, and comms/ID DIP switches on the battery.
State shows Idle instead of Charging/Discharging: check system configuration and the DC connection.
“Battery Internal Fault” shown: note the Fault # and Modbus ID, and escalate with those details.

res-lv-blown-fuse.title: LV battery blown fuse
res-lv-blown-fuse.summary: 0V across DC terminals typically confirms a blown fuse.
steps: Check DIP switches are at the recommended position.
Check for a dead short across the inverter terminals.
Photograph the DC terminal voltage and send to [contact email removed], then submit the RMA.
Note the likely cause: inverter dead short, wrong connection, external equipment fault, or wiring short circuit.

res-lv-swelling.title: LV battery swelling
res-lv-swelling.summary: Photograph and measure before lodging a claim.
steps: Photograph the battery, serial number, and setup/clearances; send to [contact email removed].
> 5mm → switch off + raise RMA. < 3mm → leave on + raise RMA.
Note: a separate source says ‘raise an RMA only if swelling exceeds 2mm’ — treat 2mm as the conservative trigger if borderline.

res-lv-cell-imbalance.title: LV battery cell imbalance
res-lv-cell-imbalance.summary: Check the inverter's own fault code for confirmation.
steps: Sungrow: Fault 937, 868. SolaX: “Batt Cell Imbalance”. GoodWe/LG: contact GoodWe for logs, refer to LGES.

res-lv-6.4ex-blinking.title: RESU 6.4EX status light blinking
res-lv-6.4ex-blinking.summary: Check DC voltage if lights blink green/orange with no inverter-side fault.
steps: If DC voltage is within 45.2V–58.1V and the light is still blinking, the battery is faulty → send RMA.

res-hv-charger.title: HV loan charger — manual charging procedure
res-hv-charger.summary: Full step-by-step procedure, voltage table, and the request/dispatch process.
steps: See Device Reference Library → HV Battery Charger for the complete procedure and the RESU7H/RESU10H voltage table.

If a charger hasn't been dispatched yet, follow the request/dispatch workflow: troubleshoot → raise ticket → send HV Charger Form → keep the ticket in your name until the form is returned → then assign to KJ.

res-fault-code-lookup.title: Use the Fault Code Lookup tab
res-fault-code-lookup.summary: Search by the exact code/number you have across SMA, SolarEdge/LGESAU, GoodWe/LGES 5048 and EM048 systems.
steps: Open the Fault Code Lookup tab and type the code or a keyword from the fault title.

res-ticket-workflow.title: Ticket & RMA workflow
res-ticket-workflow.summary: See the full reconstructed workflow diagram and key decision points.
steps: Open the RMA & Ticket Workflow tab for the stage-by-stage diagram: New → Triage/Troubleshoot → LG Approval → Charger → Job to Complete → Post Validation → Closed.

ticketWorkflow.title: LG warranty ticket workflow
ticketWorkflow.sourceNote: Reconstructed from the internal ticket/RMA swimlane flowchart (stages: New → Triage/Troubleshoot → LG Approval → Charger → Job To Complete → Post Validation → Closed; lanes: Remote Services, LGESAU, 3rd Party/Field Services, Recall, Business Services). Redrawn here for clarity — always confirm exact current field names in Odoo/Mastersheet.

stages.name: New
steps: Inbound call received.
New Call Log created (Odoo / Mastersheet).
Define Ticket Scope.
stages.branch: If the case is an LG recall case, it branches off here into an “LG Recall Case” record (Recall lane) instead of following the standard path.

stages.name: Triage / Troubleshoot
steps: Conduct Remote Troubleshooting.
Decision: Issue Resolved Remotely?
stages.branch: YES → skip straight through to ticket/call-log closure (no RMA/field work needed). NO → Create Ticket (Odoo/Mastersheet) and continue.

stages.name: LG Approval
steps: Decision: Is the issue warrantable?
If NO → “Warranty / further investigation needed” — loops back into remote troubleshooting for another pass.
If YES → Decision: Escalation required?
If escalation is needed → Technical Liaison Escalation → LGESAU RMA Procedure (which can loop back into another round of remote troubleshooting), or go straight to Raise RMA.

stages.name: Charger
steps: Decision: Charger Needed?
YES → Send Charger (see the HV Charger dispatch workflow — keep the ticket in your name until the completed HV Charger Form is returned, then assign to KJ).
NO → Enter Goods Tracking (NZ only) → Process Service Request / Work Order.

stages.name: Job To Complete
steps: From the Service Request / Work Order: either Ship Stock directly, or schedule a Field Service Visit.
After a Field Service Visit, faulty goods go through Goods Return (WH only).

stages.name: Post Validation
steps: Field / Asset Validation.
Invoicing.
Close out Goods Tracking (NZ only) — faulty stock is then returned to LG.
Decision: CX satisfaction?
stages.branch: NO → loops back to re-open the Service Request / Work Order. YES → proceed to Close Ticket.

stages.name: Closed
steps: Close of Call Log (runs in parallel for the remotely-resolved path).
Close Ticket.
Decision: Ticket Reopened? — if reopened, it loops back into the CX satisfaction check.

keyRules: Do not assign the ticket to KJ until the completed HV Charger Form has been received — keep it in your own name until then.
An issue resolved remotely never needs an RMA, a charger, or field service — it closes straight out of the Triage stage.
“Warranty / further investigation needed” is not a dead end — it loops back into another troubleshooting pass, it doesn't automatically become an RMA.
Technical Liaison Escalation and the LGESAU RMA Procedure can both send the case back for another round of remote troubleshooting before an RMA is finally raised.
Goods Tracking fields are NZ-only steps in this workflow.
